1. PATTERN OVERVIEW
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 1.1 VARIATIONAL INFERENCE PATTERN                                           │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

DESCRIPTION:
  Approximates intractable posterior distributions p(z|x) with tractable 
  variational distributions q(z|x).

KEY COMPONENTS:
  • Encoder (Recognition Model): q(z|x) - maps input to latent distribution
  • Decoder (Generative Model): p(x|z) - reconstructs input from latent
  • Reparameterization: Enables gradient flow through sampling
  • ELBO: Evidence Lower Bound as training objective

MATHEMATICAL FOUNDATION:
  log p(x) ≥ E_q[log p(x|z)] - KL(q(z|x) || p(z))
  
WHEN TO USE:
  ✓ Unsupervised learning
  ✓ Dimensionality reduction
  ✓ Generative modeling
  ✓ Learning disentangled representations
  ✗ When interpretability of latents is not needed
  ✗ When computational resources are very limited

CODE EXAMPLE:
  model = VariationalInferenceNetwork(input_dim=784, latent_dim=20)
  reconstruction, mu, logvar = model(x)
  loss = model.variational_loss(x, reconstruction, mu, logvar)

HYPERPARAMETERS:
  • latent_dim: 10-100 (depends on data complexity)
  • beta (KL weight): 0.1-1.0 (use annealing)
  • learning_rate: 1e-4 to 1e-3

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 1.2 BAYESIAN LAYER PATTERN                                                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

DESCRIPTION:
  Treats neural network weights as distributions rather than point estimates,
  providing principled uncertainty quantification.

KEY COMPONENTS:
  • Weight Distributions: Each weight has mean (μ) and variance (σ²)
  • Sampling: Sample weights during forward pass
  • KL Divergence: Regularizes weight distributions toward prior

MATHEMATICAL FOUNDATION:
  p(y|x,D) = ∫ p(y|x,w) p(w|D) dw
  Approximated by: p(w|D) ≈ q(w|θ)

WHEN TO USE:
  ✓ Small datasets (< 10k samples)
  ✓ Safety-critical applications
  ✓ When calibrated uncertainty is crucial
  ✓ Active learning scenarios
  ✗ Very large models (memory intensive)
  ✗ When fast training is priority

CODE EXAMPLE:
  layer = BayesianLinear(in_features=100, out_features=50)
  output = layer(x, sample=True)  # Sample weights
  kl_loss = layer.kl_divergence()
  total_loss = nll + kl_weight * kl_loss

HYPERPARAMETERS:
  • prior_sigma: 1.0 (standard normal prior)
  • kl_weight: 1e-4 to 1e-3 (scale by dataset size)
  • num_samples: 5-10 (training), 50-100 (inference)

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 1.3 MONTE CARLO DROPOUT PATTERN                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

DESCRIPTION:
  Uses dropout at test time to approximate Bayesian inference through
  multiple stochastic forward passes.

KEY COMPONENTS:
  • Dropout Layers: Keep active during inference
  • Multiple Samples: Run multiple forward passes
  • Uncertainty Estimation: Variance across samples

MATHEMATICAL FOUNDATION:
  Approximates variational inference with Bernoulli distributions
  q(w) = Bernoulli(1-p) for each weight

WHEN TO USE:
  ✓ Quick uncertainty estimates needed
  ✓ Retrofitting existing models
  ✓ Production systems (fast training)
  ✓ Limited computational budget
  ✗ When high-quality calibration is critical
  ✗ Very small datasets

CODE EXAMPLE:
  model = MonteCarloDropout(input_dim=784, hidden_dim=128, output_dim=10)
  mean, std = model.mc_predict(x, num_samples=100)
  entropy = model.predictive_entropy(x)

HYPERPARAMETERS:
  • dropout_rate: 0.3-0.5
  • num_mc_samples: 50-100 (evaluation), 1-5 (training)
  • Always use model.train() during MC sampling

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 1.4 REPARAMETERIZATION TRICK PATTERN                                        │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

DESCRIPTION:
  Enables gradient flow through stochastic sampling by expressing random
  variables as deterministic transformations of noise.

KEY COMPONENTS:
  • Noise Sampling: Sample ε from simple distribution
  • Deterministic Transform: z = μ + σ * ε
  • Gradient Flow: Gradients flow through μ and σ

MATHEMATICAL FOUNDATION:
  Instead of: z ~ N(μ, σ²)
  Use: z = μ + σ * ε, where ε ~ N(0, 1)

WHEN TO USE:
  ✓ Training any variational model
  ✓ Discrete latent variables (Gumbel-Softmax)
  ✓ Custom probabilistic layers
  ✓ Differentiable sampling needed
  ✗ When sampling is not part of computation graph

CODE EXAMPLE:
  reparam = ReparameterizationModule(latent_dim=20)
  z = reparam.gaussian_reparam(mu, logvar)
  z_discrete = reparam.gumbel_softmax_reparam(logits, temperature=0.5)

SUPPORTED DISTRIBUTIONS:
  • Gaussian: z = μ + σ * ε
  • Log-Normal: z = exp(μ + σ * ε)
  • Gumbel-Softmax: For categorical variables
  • Kumaraswamy: For [0,1] bounded variables

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 1.5 EVIDENCE LOWER BOUND (ELBO) PATTERN                                     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

DESCRIPTION:
  Training objective for variational inference that provides a tractable
  lower bound on the log marginal likelihood.

KEY COMPONENTS:
  • Reconstruction Term: E_q[log p(x|z)]
  • KL Divergence Term: KL(q(z|x) || p(z))
  • Beta Weight: Controls trade-off (β-VAE)

MATHEMATICAL FOUNDATION:
  ELBO = E_q[log p(x|z)] - KL(q(z|x) || p(z))
  log p(x) ≥ ELBO

WHEN TO USE:
  ✓ Training VAEs
  ✓ Any variational inference problem
  ✓ When need to balance reconstruction vs regularization
  ✓ Disentanglement learning (β-VAE)
  ✗ When exact likelihood is tractable

CODE EXAMPLE:
  elbo_loss = ELBOLoss(reconstruction_type='gaussian', beta=1.0)
  loss, metrics = elbo_loss(x, reconstruction, mu, logvar)
  
  # Beta-VAE for disentanglement
  elbo_beta = ELBOLoss(beta=4.0)  # Higher beta = more disentanglement

HYPERPARAMETERS:
  • beta: 0.1-4.0 (1.0 = standard VAE, >1 = β-VAE)
  • reconstruction_type: 'gaussian' or 'bernoulli'
  • Use KL annealing to prevent posterior collapse

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 1.6 NORMALIZING FLOW PATTERN                                                │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

DESCRIPTION:
  Transforms simple distributions into complex ones through a sequence of
  invertible transformations with tractable Jacobians.

KEY COMPONENTS:
  • Flow Layers: Invertible transformations f(z)
  • Log Determinants: Track volume changes
  • Base Distribution: Simple distribution (e.g., Gaussian)

MATHEMATICAL FOUNDATION:
  log p(z_K) = log p(z_0) - Σ log|det J_i|
  where J_i is Jacobian of i-th transformation

WHEN TO USE:
  ✓ Complex posterior approximations
  ✓ Flexible density estimation
  ✓ When simple Gaussians insufficient
  ✓ Generative modeling
  ✗ Very high-dimensional data (slow)
  ✗ Limited computational resources

CODE EXAMPLE:
  flow = NormalizingFlow(dim=20, num_flows=8, flow_type='planar')
  z_transformed, log_det = flow(z_base)
  samples = flow.sample(num_samples=100)

FLOW TYPES:
  • Planar: f(z) = z + u * tanh(w^T z + b)
  • Ra
```python
dial: f(z) = z + β * h(α, r) * (z - z_0)
  • RealNVP: Coupling layers for high dimensions
  • Autoregressive: MAF/IAF for flexible modeling

HYPERPARAMETERS:
  • num_flows: 4-16 layers
  • flow_type: 'planar' (simple), 'radial' (radial symmetry)
  • learning_rate: 1e-4 (flows need careful tuning)

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
2. IMPLEMENTATION DETAILS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 2.1 COMMON PITFALLS AND SOLUTIONS                                           │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

PITFALL #1: KL Divergence Collapse
  SYMPTOM: KL term goes to zero, model ignores latent variables
  CAUSES:
    • Too strong KL weight
    • Decoder too powerful
    • Learning rate too high
  SOLUTIONS:
    ✓ Use KL annealing (start beta=0, increase gradually)
    ✓ Free bits: max(KL, threshold) per latent dimension
    ✓ Reduce decoder capacity
    ✓ Increase latent dimension

PITFALL #2: Poor Calibration
  SYMPTOM: Model overconfident or underconfident
  CAUSES:
    • Insufficient MC samples
    • Wrong prior assumptions
    • Training data imbalance
  SOLUTIONS:
    ✓ Temperature scaling post-training
    ✓ Increase MC samples (50-100)
    ✓ Use proper scoring rules
    ✓ Validate on calibration set

PITFALL #3: Numerical Instability
  SYMPTOM: NaN losses, exploding gradients
  CAUSES:
    • Log of zero/negative values
    • Large log determinants in flows
    • Extreme parameter values
  SOLUTIONS:
    ✓ Add epsilon (1e-8) to logs
    ✓ Gradient clipping (max_norm=1.0)
    ✓ Use log-space computations
    ✓ Initialize carefully

PITFALL #4: Slow Training/Inference
  SYMPTOM: Training takes too long
  CAUSES:
    • Too many MC samples
    • Large flow models
    • Inefficient sampling
  SOLUTIONS:
    ✓ Reduce samples during training (1-5)
    ✓ Use local reparameterization trick
    ✓ Batch operations efficiently
    ✓ Consider model distillation

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 2.2 ADVANCED TECHNIQUES                                                     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

TECHNIQUE #1: Importance Weighted ELBO (IWAE)
  PURPOSE: Tighter bound on log-likelihood
  IMPLEMENTATION:
    iwae_loss = ImportanceWeightedELBO(num_samples=5)
    loss = iwae_loss(x, encoder, decoder, reparam_fn)
  BENEFITS:
    • Better density estimation
    • Improved sample quality
  COST: 5-10x slower training

TECHNIQUE #2: Variational Dropout
  PURPOSE: Learn optimal dropout rates per parameter
  IMPLEMENTATION:
    layer = VariationalDropout(input_dim=100, output_dim=50)
    output = layer(x)
    kl = layer.kl_divergence()
  BENEFITS:
    • Automatic network pruning
    • Better uncertainty
  COST: Slightly more memory

TECHNIQUE #3: Concrete Dropout
  PURPOSE: Automatically tune dropout rates
  IMPLEMENTATION:
    concrete = ConcreteDropout()
    output = concrete(x, layer)
    reg = concrete.regularization(layer)
  BENEFITS:
    • No manual tuning
    • Task-adaptive
  COST: Small computational overhead

TECHNIQUE #4: Stochastic Weight Averaging
  PURPOSE: Better generalization and calibration
  IMPLEMENTATION:
    swa = StochasticWeightAveraging(model, swa_start=5)
    # During training:
    swa.update()
    # After training:
    final_model = swa.get_swa_model()
  BENEFITS:
    • Improved calibration
    • Better generalization
  COST: Minimal

3. USAGE EXAMPLES
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 3.1 BASIC CLASSIFICATION WITH UNCERTAINTY                                   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

# Setup
model = BayesianNetwork(input_dim=784, hidden_dim=128, output_dim=10)
optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3)

# Training loop
for epoch in range(num_epochs):
    for batch_x, batch_y in train_loader:
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        
        # Forward with weight sampling
        output = model(batch_x, sample=True)
        nll = F.cross_entropy(output, batch_y)
        kl = model.kl_divergence() / len(train_dataset)
        
        loss = nll + 1e-4 * kl
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()

# Inference with uncertainty
model.eval()
predictions = []
for _ in range(100):  # 100 MC samples
    pred = F.softmax(model(test_x, sample=True), dim=-1)
    predictions.append(pred)

predictions = torch.stack(predictions)
mean_pred = predictions.mean(dim=0)
uncertainty = predictions.std(dim=0)

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 3.2 GENERATIVE MODELING WITH VAE + FLOWS                                    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

# Setup
model = FlowBasedVAE(input_dim=784, latent_dim=20, num_flows=4)
optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3)
scheduler = ELBOScheduler(n_epochs=100, anneal_type='cyclical')

# Training
for epoch in range(100):
    for batch_x, _ in train_loader:
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        
        reconstruction, mu, logvar, log_det = model(batch_x)
        loss = model.loss_function(batch_x, reconstruction, mu, logvar, log_det)
        
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
    
    scheduler.step()

# Generation
with torch.no_grad():
    samples = model.flows.sample(num_samples=64)
    generated = model.decode(samples)

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 3.3 ANOMALY DETECTION                                                       │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

# Setup
detector = AnomalyDetector(input_dim=784, latent_dim=16, num_flows=4)

# Train on normal data
for epoch in range(50):
    for normal_batch, _ in normal_data_loader:
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        reconstruction, mu, logvar, log_det = detector(normal_batch)
        loss = detector.vae.loss_function(normal_batch, reconstruction, 
                                         mu, logvar, log_det)
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()

# Calibrate threshold
detector.calibrate(normal_data_loader, percentile=95)

# Detect anomalies
is_anomaly, scores = detector.detect_anomalies(test_data)
print(f"Detected {is_anomaly.sum()} anomalies out of {len(test_data)}")

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 3.4 ACTIVE LEARNING                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

# Initial training on small labeled set
model = BayesianNetwork(input_dim=784, hidden_dim=128, output_dim=10)
train_model(model, small_labeled_data)

# Active learning loop
for iteration in range(num_iterations):
    # Get uncertainty on unlabeled pool
    uncertainties = []
    for batch in unlabeled_pool:
        _, epistemic, _, total = model.predict_with_uncertainty(batch)
        uncertainties.append(total.mean(dim=-1))
    
    uncertainties = torch.cat(uncertainties)
    
    # Select most uncertain samples
    top_k_indices = torch.topk(uncertainties, k=batch_size).indices
    
    # Query oracle for labels
    new_labeled_data = query_oracle(unlabeled_pool[top_k_indices])
    
    # Retrain model
    labeled_data = torch.cat([labeled_data, new_labeled_data])
    train_model(model, labeled_data)

4. BEST PRACTICES
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 4.1 TRAINING GUIDELINES                                                     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

✓ DO:
  • Start with simple baselines (MC Dropout)
  • Monitor KL and reconstruction separately
  • Use gradient clipping (max_norm=1.0)
  • Validate uncertainty on held-out calibration set
  • Use early stopping based on calibration metrics
  • Save multiple checkpoints throughout training
  • Use mixed precision training for large models
  • Log all hyperparameters and random seeds

✗ DON'T:
  • Use KL weight > 1 without annealing
  • Ignore calibration metrics
  • Skip validation on OOD data
  • Use too few MC samples for evaluation
  • Forget to set model.train() for MC Dropout
  • Assume uncertainty is well-calibrated
  • Use default hyperparameters without tuning

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 4.2 HYPERPARAMETER TUNING GUIDE                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

LEARNING RATE:
  • Bayesian models: 1e-4 to 1e-3
  • VAE/Flows: 1e-4 (more sensitive)
  • Use ReduceLROnPlateau scheduler
  • Warmup for first 5-10% of training

KL WEIGHT:
  • Start: 0 or 1e-5
  • End: 1e-4 to 1e-3
  • Scale inversely with dataset size
  • Use cyclical annealing for better exploration

LATENT DIMENSION:
  • Small datasets: 10-20
  • Medium datasets: 20-50
  • Large datasets: 50-100
  • Rule of thumb: ~1-5% of input dimension

NUMBER OF FLOWS:
  • Start with 4-8 layers
  • Add more if posterior is complex
  • Diminishing returns after 16 layers
  • Each layer adds ~10% training time

MC SAMPLES:
  • Training: 1-5 samples
  • Validation: 10-20 samples
  • Testing: 50-100 samples
  • Critical decisions: 100-500 samples

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 4.3 DEBUGGING CHECKLIST                                                     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

□ Check data normalization (zero mean, unit variance)
□ Verify loss components are in reasonable ranges
□ Monitor gradient norms (should be 0.1-10)
□ Check for NaN/Inf in outputs
□ Validate KL doesn't collapse to zero
□ Ensure dropout is active during MC sampling
□ Verify temperature scaling improves ECE
□ Test on simple synthetic data first
□ Compare to deterministic baseline
□ Visualize latent space (for VAEs)
□ Plot calibration curves
□ Check uncertainty on known OOD data

  • Apply mixed precision training (torch.cuda.amp)
  • Reduce batch size, increase gradient accumulation
  • Use local reparameterization for Bayesian layers
  • Clear cache regularly: torch.cuda.empty_cache()

SPEED OPTIMIZATION:

  • Use DataLoader with num_workers > 0
  • Pin memory for GPU training
  • Batch operations whenever possible
  • Use einsum for complex tensor operations
  • Profile code with torch.profiler

INFERENCE OPTIMIZATION:
  • Export to ONNX for production
  • Apply dynamic quantization
  • Use TorchScript tracing
  • Batch predictions
  • Cache encoder outputs (for VAEs)
  • Use fewer MC samples for non-critical predictions

8. APPENDIX: MATHEMATICAL FOUNDATIONS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

VARIATIONAL INFERENCE:
  Objective: Minimize KL(q(z|x) || p(z|x))
  ELBO: log p(x) ≥ E_q[log p(x|z)] - KL(q(z|x) || p(z))
  
  Derivation:
    log p(x) = log ∫ p(x,z) dz
             = log ∫ p(x,z) q(z|x)/q(z|x) dz
             = log E_q[p(x,z)/q(z|x)]
             ≥ E_q[log p(x,z)/q(z|x)]  (Jensen's inequality)
             = E_q[log p(x|z)] - KL(q(z|x) || p(z))

BAYESIAN NEURAL NETWORKS:
  Posterior: p(w|D) = p(D|w)p(w) / p(D)
  Predictive: p(y*|x*,D) = ∫ p(y*|x*,w) p(w|D) dw
  
  Variational approximation:
    q(w|θ) ≈ p(w|D)
    Minimize: KL(q(w|θ) || p(w|D))
    Equivalent to maximizing: E_q[log p(D|w)] - KL(q(w|θ) || p(w))

NORMALIZING FLOWS:
  Change of variables:
    p_K(z_K) = p_0(z_0) |det(∂z_0/∂z_K)|
    
  Log-likelihood:
    log p_K(z_K) = log p_0(z_0) - Σ_{k=1}^K log|det J_k|
    
  where J_k = ∂f_k/∂z_{k-1} is the Jacobian

REPARAMETERIZATION TRICK:
  Original: z ~ q(z|x)
  Reparameterized: z = g(ε, x) where ε ~ p(ε)
  
  Gradient:
    ∇_θ E_q[f(z)] = E_p[∇_θ f(g(ε, x))]
  
  Enables backpropagation through sampling

## 1. Attention-Based Selection Pattern

```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F
from typing import Tuple, Optional

class AttentionBasedFeatureSelector(nn.Module):
    """
    Attention-Based Feature Selection Pattern
    
    Uses attention mechanism to dynamically weight and select important features.
    The attention scores indicate feature importance and can be used for selection.
    
    Args:
        input_dim: Number of input features
        hidden_dim: Dimension of attention hidden layer
        num_heads: Number of attention heads for multi-head attention
        dropout: Dropout rate for regularization
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self, 
        input_dim: int, 
        hidden_dim: int = 64,
        num_heads: int = 4,
        dropout: float = 0.1
    ):
        super(AttentionBasedFeatureSelector, self).__init__()
        
        self.input_dim = input_dim
        self.hidden_dim = hidden_dim
        self.num_heads = num_heads
        
        # Multi-head attention for feature selection
        self.attention = nn.MultiheadAttention(
            embed_dim=input_dim,
            num_heads=num_heads,
            dropout=dropout,
            batch_first=True
        )
        
        # Alternative: Self-attention mechanism
        self.query = nn.Linear(input_dim, hidden_dim)
        self.key = nn.Linear(input_dim, hidden_dim)
        self.value = nn.Linear(input_dim, hidden_dim)
        
        # Feature importance scorer
        self.importance_scorer = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(input_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, 1),
            nn.Sigmoid()
        )
        
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout)
        
    def forward(
        self, 
        x: torch.Tensor, 
        return_attention: bool = False
    ) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, Optional[torch.Tensor]]:
        """
        Forward pass with attention-based feature selection
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor of shape (batch_size, num_features)
            return_attention: Whether to return attention weights
            
        Returns:
            selected_features: Weighted features
            attention_weights: Optional attention weights for interpretability
        """
        batch_size = x.shape[0]
        
        # Reshape for attention mechanism (batch, seq_len=1, features)
        x_reshaped = x.unsqueeze(1)
        
        # Apply multi-head attention
        attn_output, attn_weights = self.attention(
            x_reshaped, x_reshaped, x_reshaped
        )
        attn_output = attn_output.squeeze(1)
        
        # Compute feature importance scores
        importance_scores = self.importance_scorer(x)  # (batch_size, 1)
        
        # Weight features by importance
        selected_features = x * importance_scores
        
        # Combine with attention output
        combined_features = selected_features + self.dropout(attn_output)
        
        if return_attention:
            return combined_features, attn_weights.squeeze(1)
        return combined_features, None
    
    def get_feature_importance(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Get feature importance scores for interpretability
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor
            
        Returns:
            Feature importance scores
        """
        with torch.no_grad():
            importance = self.importance_scorer(x)
        return importance


# Example usage
def example_attention_based_selection():
    """Example demonstrating attention-based feature selection"""
    
    # Create sample data
    batch_size = 32
    num_features = 100
    x = torch.randn(batch_size, num_features)
    
    # Initialize model
    selector = AttentionBasedFeatureSelector(
        input_dim=num_features,
        hidden_dim=64,
        num_heads=4,
        dropout=0.1
    )
    
    # Forward pass
    selected_features, attention_weights = selector(x, return_attention=True)
    
    print(f"Input shape: {x.shape}")
    print(f"Selected features shape: {selected_features.shape}")
    print(f"Attention weights shape: {attention_weights.shape}")
    
    # Get feature importance
    importance = selector.get_feature_importance(x)
    print(f"Feature importance shape: {importance.shape}")
    print(f"Top 5 important features: {importance.mean(0).topk(5).indices}")

```

## 2. Gating-Based Selection Pattern

```python
class GatingBasedFeatureSelector(nn.Module):
    """
    Gating-Based Feature Selection Pattern
    
    Uses learnable gates to control information flow from each feature.
    Gates are computed dynamically based on input, allowing adaptive selection.
    
    Args:
        input_dim: Number of input features
        hidden_dim: Hidden dimension for gate computation
        gate_type: Type of gate ('sigmoid', 'softmax', 'sparsemax')
        temperature: Temperature for softmax/sparsemax gates
        dropout: Dropout rate
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        input_dim: int,
        hidden_dim: int = 64,
        gate_type: str = 'sigmoid',
        temperature: float = 1.0,
        dropout: float = 0.1
    ):
        super(GatingBasedFeatureSelector, self).__init__()
        
        self.input_dim = input_dim
        self.gate_type = gate_type
        self.temperature = temperature
        
        # Gate network - computes gating values for each feature
        self.gate_network = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(input_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, hidden_dim // 2),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim // 2, input_dim)
        )
        
        # Feature transformation network
        self.feature_transform = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(input_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, input_dim)
        )
        
        # Learnable feature-specific parameters
        self.feature_bias = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(input_dim))
        
    def compute_gates(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Compute gating values for features
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor
            
        Returns:
            Gate values in range [0, 1]
        """
        # Compute raw gate logits
        gate_logits = self.gate_network(x) + self.feature_bias
        
        # Apply gating function based on type
        if self.gate_type == 'sigmoid':
            gates = torch.sigmoid(gate_logits / self.temperature)
        elif self.gate_type == 'softmax':
            gates = F.softmax(gate_logits / self.temperature, dim=-1)
        elif self.gate_type == 'sparsemax':
            gates = self._sparsemax(gate_logits / self.temperature)
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown gate type: {self.gate_type}")
            
        return gates
    
    def _sparsemax(self, z: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Sparsemax activation (produces sparse probability distributions)
        
        Args:
            z: Input logits
            
        Returns:
            Sparse probability distribution
        """
        # Sort input in descending order
        z_sorted, _ = torch.sort(z, dim=-1, descending=True)
        
        # Compute cumulative sum
        z_cumsum = torch.cumsum(z_sorted, dim=-1)
        
        # Find threshold
        k = torch.arange(1, z.shape[-1] + 1, device=z.device).float()
        z_check = 1 + k * z_sorted > z_cumsum
        
        # Get k_z (number of non-zero elements)
        k_z = z_check.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
        
        # Compute threshold tau
        tau_z = (z_cumsum.gather(-1, k_z - 1) - 1) / k_z.float()
        
        # Apply threshold
        output = torch.clamp(z - tau_z, min=0)
        
        return output
    
    def forward(
        self, 
        x: torch.Tensor,
        return_gates: bool = False
    ) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, Optional[torch.Tensor]]:
        """
        Forward pass with gating-based feature selection
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor of shape (batch_size, num_features)
            return_gates: Whether to return gate values
            
        Returns:
            selected_features: Gated features
            gates: Optional gate values
        """
        # Compute gates
        gates = self.compute_gates(x)
        
        # Transform features
        transformed_features = self.feature_transform(x)
        
        # Apply gates to select features
        selected_features = gates * transformed_features
        
        if return_gates:
            return selected_features, gates
        return selected_features, None
    
    def get_feature_selection_mask(
        self, 
        x: torch.Tensor, 
        threshold: float = 0.5
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Get binary feature selection mask based on gate values
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor
            threshold: Threshold for binary selection
            
        Returns:
            Binary mask indicating selected features
        """
        with torch.no_grad():
            gates = self.compute_gates(x)
            mask = (gates > threshold).float()
        return mask


# Example usage
def example_gating_based_selection():
    """Example demonstrating gating-based feature selection"""
    
    # Create sample data
    batch_size = 32
    num_features = 100
    x = torch.randn(batch_size, num_features)
    
    # Test different gate types
    for gate_type in ['sigmoid', 'softmax', 'sparsemax']:
        print(f"\n--- Testing {gate_type} gates ---")
        
        selector = GatingBasedFeatureSelector(
            input_dim=num_features,
            hidden_dim=64,
            gate_type=gate_type,
            temperature=1.0,
            dropout=0.1
        )
        
        # Forward pass
        selected_features, gates = selector(x, return_gates=True)
        
        print(f"Input shape: {x.shape}")
        print(f"Selected features shape: {selected_features.shape}")
        print(f"Gates shape: {gates.shape}")
        print(f"Gates mean: {gates.mean().item():.4f}")
        print(f"Gates std: {gates.std().item():.4f}")
        print(f"Sparsity (zeros): {(gates < 0.01).float().mean().item():.4f}")
        
        # Get selection mask
        mask = selector.get_feature_selection_mask(x, threshold=0.5)
        print(f"Selected features: {mask.sum(dim=1).float().mean().item():.2f}/{num_features}")

```

## 3. L1 Regularization Selection Pattern

```python
class L1RegularizedFeatureSelector(nn.Module):
    """
    L1 Regularization-Based Feature Selection Pattern
    
    Uses L1 regularization to encourage sparse feature weights.
    Features with weights close to zero can be pruned.
    
    Args:
        input_dim: Number of input features
        output_dim: Output dimension
        hidden_dims: List of hidden layer dimensions
        l1_lambda: L1 regularization strength
        dropout: Dropout rate
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        input_dim: int,
        output_dim: int,
        hidden_dims: list = [128, 64],
        l1_lambda: float = 0.01,
        dropout: float = 0.1
    ):
        super(L1RegularizedFeatureSelector, self).__init__()
        
        self.input_dim = input_dim
        self.output_dim = output_dim
        self.l1_lambda = l1_lambda
        
        # Feature weight layer (for L1 regularization)
        self.feature_weights = nn.Parameter(torch.ones(input_dim))
        
        # Build network layers
        layers = []
        prev_dim = input_dim
        
        for hidden_dim in hidden_dims:
            layers.extend([
                nn.Linear(prev_dim, hidden_dim),
                nn.BatchNorm1d(hidden_dim),
                nn.ReLU(),
                nn.Dropout(dropout)
            ])
            prev_dim = hidden_dim
        
        # Output layer
        layers.append(nn.Linear(prev_dim, output_dim))
        
        self.network = nn.Sequential(*layers)
        
        # Track selected features
        self.register_buffer('selected_features_mask', torch.ones(input_dim))
        
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Forward pass with L1-weighted features
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor of shape (batch_size, num_features)
            
        Returns:
            Output predictions
        """
        # Apply learned feature weights
        weighted_x = x * torch.abs(self.feature_weights)
        
        # Pass through network
        output = self.network(weighted_x)
        
        return output
    
    def compute_l1_loss(self) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Compute L1 regularization loss on feature weights
        
        Returns:
            L1 loss value
        """
        return self.l1_lambda * torch.sum(torch.abs(self.feature_weights))
    
    def get_feature_importance(self) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Get feature importance based on learned weights
        
        Returns:
            Feature importance scores
        """
        with torch.no_grad():
            importance = torch.abs(self.feature_weights)
        return importance
    
    def prune_features(self, threshold: float = 0.01) -> int:
        """
        Prune features with weights below threshold
        
        Args:
            threshold: Minimum weight threshold
            
        Returns:
            Number of features pruned
        """
        with torch.no_grad():
            importance = torch.abs(self.feature_weights)
            mask = (importance > threshold).float()
            
            # Update mask
            self.selected_features_mask = mask
            
            # Zero out pruned weights
            self.feature_weights.data *= mask
            
            num_pruned = (mask == 0).sum().item()
            
        return num_pruned
    
    def get_selected_features(self) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Get indices of selected (non-pruned) features
        
        Returns:
            Indices of selected features
        """
        return torch.where(self.selected_features_mask > 0)[0]


# Example usage with training loop
def example_l1_regularization_selection():
    """Example demonstrating L1 regularization-based feature selection"""
    
    # Create sample data
    batch_size = 32
    num_features = 100
    output_dim = 10
    
```python
    # Create sample data with some irrelevant features
    x_train = torch.randn(batch_size * 10, num_features)
    # Make only first 30 features relevant
    y_train = torch.sum(x_train[:, :30], dim=1, keepdim=True)
    y_train = (y_train > 0).long().squeeze()
    y_train = F.one_hot(y_train, num_classes=output_dim).float()
    
    # Initialize model
    selector = L1RegularizedFeatureSelector(
        input_dim=num_features,
        output_dim=output_dim,
        hidden_dims=[128, 64],
        l1_lambda=0.01,
        dropout=0.1
    )
    
    # Training setup
    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(selector.parameters(), lr=0.001)
    criterion = nn.MSELoss()
    
    print("Training with L1 regularization...")
    num_epochs = 50
    
    for epoch in range(num_epochs):
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        
        # Forward pass
        output = selector(x_train)
        
        # Compute losses
        prediction_loss = criterion(output, y_train)
        l1_loss = selector.compute_l1_loss()
        total_loss = prediction_loss + l1_loss
        
        # Backward pass
        total_loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
        
        if (epoch + 1) % 10 == 0:
            print(f"Epoch {epoch+1}/{num_epochs}")
            print(f"  Prediction Loss: {prediction_loss.item():.4f}")
            print(f"  L1 Loss: {l1_loss.item():.4f}")
            print(f"  Total Loss: {total_loss.item():.4f}")
    
    # Analyze feature selection
    print("\n--- Feature Selection Results ---")
    importance = selector.get_feature_importance()
    print(f"Feature importance range: [{importance.min():.4f}, {importance.max():.4f}]")
    
    # Prune features
    num_pruned = selector.prune_features(threshold=0.1)
    print(f"Features pruned: {num_pruned}/{num_features}")
    
    selected_indices = selector.get_selected_features()
    print(f"Selected features: {len(selected_indices)}")
    print(f"Top 10 selected feature indices: {selected_indices[:10].tolist()}")
    
    # Show top important features
    top_k = 10
    top_indices = torch.argsort(importance, descending=True)[:top_k]
    print(f"\nTop {top_k} important features:")
    for i, idx in enumerate(top_indices):
        print(f"  {i+1}. Feature {idx.item()}: {importance[idx].item():.4f}")

## 4. Learned Feature Selection Pattern

```python
class LearnedFeatureSelector(nn.Module):
    """
    Learned Feature Selection Pattern
    
    Learns to select a fixed number of features using differentiable selection.
    Uses concrete/Gumbel-Softmax for differentiable sampling during training.
    
    Args:
        input_dim: Number of input features
        num_select: Number of features to select
        hidden_dim: Hidden dimension for selection network
        temperature: Temperature for Gumbel-Softmax
        hard: Whether to use hard (discrete) selection
        dropout: Dropout rate
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        input_dim: int,
        num_select: int,
        hidden_dim: int = 64,
        temperature: float = 1.0,
        hard: bool = False,
        dropout: float = 0.1
    ):
        super(LearnedFeatureSelector, self).__init__()
        
        self.input_dim = input_dim
        self.num_select = num_select
        self.temperature = temperature
        self.hard = hard
        
        # Selection network - learns which features to select
        self.selection_network = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(input_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, input_dim)
        )
        
        # Feature embedding network
        self.feature_embedder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(input_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.LayerNorm(hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(dropout)
        )
        
        # Selection scores (learnable per-feature bias)
        self.selection_scores = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(input_dim))
        
        # Output projection
        self.output_projection = nn.Linear(hidden_dim, input_dim)
        
    def compute_selection_logits(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Compute logits for feature selection
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor
            
        Returns:
            Selection logits
        """
        # Context-dependent selection scores
        context_scores = self.selection_network(x)
        
        # Combine with learned feature-specific scores
        logits = context_scores + self.selection_scores
        
        return logits
    
    def gumbel_softmax_sample(
        self, 
        logits: torch.Tensor, 
        temperature: float = 1.0,
        hard: bool = False
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Sample from Gumbel-Softmax distribution
        
        Args:
            logits: Selection logits
            temperature: Softmax temperature
            hard: Whether to use hard (one-hot) samples
            
        Returns:
            Soft or hard selection samples
        """
        # Sample from Gumbel distribution
        gumbel_noise = -torch.log(-torch.log(
            torch.rand_like(logits) + 1e-20) + 1e-20
        )
        
        # Add Gumbel noise to logits
        noisy_logits = (logits + gumbel_noise) / temperature
        
        # Apply softmax
        soft_samples = F.softmax(noisy_logits, dim=-1)
        
        if hard:
            # Create hard one-hot samples
            _, indices = soft_samples.max(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
            hard_samples = torch.zeros_like(soft_samples)
            hard_samples.scatter_(-1, indices, 1.0)
            
            # Use straight-through estimator
            samples = hard_samples - soft_samples.detach() + soft_samples
        else:
            samples = soft_samples
            
        return samples
    
    def top_k_selection(
        self, 
        logits: torch.Tensor, 
        k: int,
        hard: bool = False
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Select top-k features
        
        Args:
            logits: Selection logits
            k: Number of features to select
            hard: Whether to use hard selection
            
        Returns:
            Selection mask
        """
        # Get top-k values and indices
        topk_values, topk_indices = torch.topk(logits, k, dim=-1)
        
        if hard:
            # Hard selection - binary mask
            mask = torch.zeros_like(logits)
            mask.scatter_(-1, topk_indices, 1.0)
        else:
            # Soft selection - use softmax over top-k
            soft_weights = F.softmax(topk_values / self.temperature, dim=-1)
            mask = torch.zeros_like(logits)
            mask.scatter_(-1, topk_indices, soft_weights)
        
        return mask
    
    def forward(
        self, 
        x: torch.Tensor,
        return_selection: bool = False
    ) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, Optional[torch.Tensor]]:
        """
        Forward pass with learned feature selection
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor of shape (batch_size, num_features)
            return_selection: Whether to return selection mask
            
        Returns:
            selected_features: Selected and transformed features
            selection_mask: Optional selection mask
        """
        # Compute selection logits
        logits = self.compute_selection_logits(x)
        
        # Select top-k features
        selection_mask = self.top_k_selection(
            logits, 
            self.num_select,
            hard=self.hard
        )
        
        # Apply selection to input
        selected_input = x * selection_mask
        
        # Embed selected features
        embedded = self.feature_embedder(selected_input)
        
        # Project back to input dimension
        output = self.output_projection(embedded)
        
        if return_selection:
            return output, selection_mask
        return output, None
    
    def get_selected_features(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Get indices of selected features
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor
            
        Returns:
            Indices of selected features
        """
        with torch.no_grad():
            logits = self.compute_selection_logits(x)
            _, indices = torch.topk(logits, self.num_select, dim=-1)
        return indices
    
    def get_feature_selection_probability(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Get probability of each feature being selected
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor
            
        Returns:
            Selection probabilities
        """
        with torch.no_grad():
            logits = self.compute_selection_logits(x)
            probs = F.softmax(logits, dim=-1)
        return probs


# Example usage
def example_learned_feature_selection():
    """Example demonstrating learned feature selection"""
    
    # Create sample data
    batch_size = 32
    num_features = 100
    num_select = 20
    x = torch.randn(batch_size, num_features)
    
    print(f"--- Learned Feature Selection ---")
    print(f"Input features: {num_features}")
    print(f"Features to select: {num_select}\n")
    
    # Test with different settings
    for hard in [False, True]:
        mode = "Hard" if hard else "Soft"
        print(f"--- {mode} Selection Mode ---")
        
        selector = LearnedFeatureSelector(
            input_dim=num_features,
            num_select=num_select,
            hidden_dim=64,
            temperature=1.0,
            hard=hard,
            dropout=0.1
        )
        
        # Forward pass
        selected_features, selection_mask = selector(x, return_selection=True)
        
        print(f"Input shape: {x.shape}")
        print(f"Output shape: {selected_features.shape}")
        print(f"Selection mask shape: {selection_mask.shape}")
        print(f"Non-zero selections per sample: {(selection_mask > 0).sum(dim=1).float().mean():.2f}")
        
        # Get selected feature indices
        indices = selector.get_selected_features(x)
        print(f"Selected feature indices shape: {indices.shape}")
        print(f"Example selected features (first sample): {indices[0][:10].tolist()}")
        
        # Get selection probabilities
        probs = selector.get_feature_selection_probability(x)
        print(f"Selection probability range: [{probs.min():.4f}, {probs.max():.4f}]")
        print(f"Top 5 features by probability: {probs.mean(0).topk(5).indices.tolist()}\n")

```

```python
class ImportanceWeightingSelector(nn.Module):
    """
    Importance Weighting Pattern for Feature Selection
    
    Learns importance weights for each feature and applies them dynamically.
    Combines multiple importance estimation strategies.
    
    Args:
        input_dim: Number of input features
        hidden_dim: Hidden dimension for importance network
        num_importance_heads: Number of different importance estimators
        use_variance: Whether to use variance-based importance
        use_gradient: Whether to use gradient-based importance
        dropout: Dropout rate
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        input_dim: int,
        hidden_dim: int = 64,
        num_importance_heads: int = 3,
        use_variance: bool = True,
        use_gradient: bool = True,
        dropout: float = 0.1
    ):
        super(ImportanceWeightingSelector, self).__init__()
        
        self.input_dim = input_dim
        self.hidden_dim = hidden_dim
        self.num_importance_heads = num_importance_heads
        self.use_variance = use_variance
        self.use_gradient = use_gradient
        
        # Multiple importance estimation heads
        self.importance_heads = nn.ModuleList([
            nn.Sequential(
                nn.Linear(input_dim, hidden_dim),
                nn.ReLU(),
                nn.Dropout(dropout),
                nn.Linear(hidden_dim, input_dim),
                nn.Sigmoid()
            ) for _ in range(num_importance_heads)
        ])
        
        # Global importance weights (learned parameters)
        self.global_importance = nn.Parameter(torch.ones(input_dim))
        
        # Feature statistics tracker
        self.register_buffer('feature_mean', torch.zeros(input_dim))
        self.register_buffer('feature_var', torch.ones(input_dim))
        self.register_buffer('num_batches_tracked', torch.tensor(0))
        
        # Importance aggregation network
        self.importance_aggregator = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(num_importance_heads, hidden_dim // 2),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim // 2, 1),
            nn.Sigmoid()
        )
        
        # Feature transformation
        self.feature_transform = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(input_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.LayerNorm(hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, input_dim)
        )
        
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout)
        
    def update_statistics(self, x: torch.Tensor, momentum: float = 0.1):
        """
        Update running statistics for variance-based importance
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor
            momentum: Momentum for running statistics
        """
        if self.training:
            with torch.no_grad():
                batch_mean = x.mean(dim=0)
                batch_var = x.var(dim=0, unbiased=False)
                
                # Update running statistics
                self.feature_mean = (1 - momentum) * self.feature_mean + momentum * batch_mean
                self.feature_var = (1 - momentum) * self.feature_var + momentum * batch_var
                self.num_batches_tracked += 1
    
    def compute_variance_importance(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Compute importance based on feature variance
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor
            
        Returns:
            Variance-based importance scores
        """
        # Features with higher variance are more important
        variance = x.var(dim=0, keepdim=True)
        importance = variance / (variance.sum() + 1e-8)
        return importance.expand(x.shape[0], -1)
    
    
```python
    def compute_gradient_importance(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Compute importance based on gradient magnitude
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor
            
        Returns:
            Gradient-based importance scores
        """
        # Compute gradient of output w.r.t. input
        if x.requires_grad:
            # Use gradient magnitude as importance
            grad_output = torch.ones_like(x)
            gradients = torch.autograd.grad(
                outputs=x.sum(),
                inputs=x,
                grad_outputs=grad_output,
                create_graph=True,
                retain_graph=True
            )[0]
            importance = torch.abs(gradients)
        else:
            # Fallback to uniform importance
            importance = torch.ones_like(x)
        
        return importance
    
    def compute_multi_head_importance(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Compute importance using multiple heads and aggregate
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor
            
        Returns:
            Aggregated importance scores
        """
        # Compute importance from each head
        head_importances = []
        for head in self.importance_heads:
            head_importance = head(x)
            head_importances.append(head_importance.unsqueeze(-1))
        
        # Stack all head importances (batch_size, input_dim, num_heads)
        stacked_importances = torch.cat(head_importances, dim=-1)
        
        # Aggregate across heads
        aggregated = self.importance_aggregator(stacked_importances).squeeze(-1)
        
        return aggregated
    
    def compute_combined_importance(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Combine multiple importance estimation strategies
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor
            
        Returns:
            Combined importance weights
        """
        importances = []
        
        # Multi-head learned importance
        head_importance = self.compute_multi_head_importance(x)
        importances.append(head_importance)
        
        # Variance-based importance
        if self.use_variance:
            var_importance = self.compute_variance_importance(x)
            importances.append(var_importance)
        
        # Global learned importance
        global_imp = torch.sigmoid(self.global_importance).unsqueeze(0).expand_as(x)
        importances.append(global_imp)
        
        # Average all importance scores
        combined = torch.stack(importances).mean(dim=0)
        
        # Normalize to sum to number of features (maintains scale)
        combined = combined / (combined.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True) + 1e-8) * self.input_dim
        
        return combined
    
    def forward(
        self, 
        x: torch.Tensor,
        return_importance: bool = False
    ) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, Optional[torch.Tensor]]:
        """
        Forward pass with importance weighting
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor of shape (batch_size, num_features)
            return_importance: Whether to return importance weights
            
        Returns:
            weighted_features: Importance-weighted features
            importance_weights: Optional importance weights
        """
        # Update statistics
        self.update_statistics(x)
        
        # Compute combined importance weights
        importance_weights = self.compute_combined_importance(x)
        
        # Apply importance weights to features
        weighted_input = x * importance_weights
        
        # Transform weighted features
        transformed = self.feature_transform(weighted_input)
        
        # Residual connection
        output = weighted_input + self.dropout(transformed)
        
        if return_importance:
            return output, importance_weights
        return output, None
    
    def get_feature_ranking(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        """
        Get feature ranking based on importance
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor
            
        Returns:
            Tuple of (importance_scores, ranked_indices)
        """
        with torch.no_grad():
            importance = self.compute_combined_importance(x)
            avg_importance = importance.mean(dim=0)
            ranked_indices = torch.argsort(avg_importance, descending=True)
        
        return avg_importance, ranked_indices
    
    def select_top_k_features(
        self, 
        x: torch.Tensor, 
        k: int
    ) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        """
        Select top-k most important features
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor
            k: Number of features to select
            
        Returns:
            Tuple of (selected_features, selected_indices)
        """
        importance, ranked_indices = self.get_feature_ranking(x)
        top_k_indices = ranked_indices[:k]
        
        # Create mask for top-k features
        mask = torch.zeros(self.input_dim, device=x.device)
        mask[top_k_indices] = 1.0
        
        # Select features
        selected_features = x * mask.unsqueeze(0)
        
        return selected_features, top_k_indices


# Example usage
def example_importance_weighting():

class FeatureSelectionPipeline(nn.Module):
    """
    Complete feature selection pipeline combining multiple patterns
    
    Args:
        input_dim: Number of input features
        output_dim: Output dimension
        selection_method: Method to use ('attention', 'gating', 'l1', 'learned', 'importance')
        num_select: Number of features to select (for learned method)
        hidden_dim: Hidden dimension
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        input_dim: int,
        output_dim: int,
        selection_method: str = 'attention',
        num_select: int = None,
        hidden_dim: int = 64
    ):
        super(FeatureSelectionPipeline, self).__init__()
        
        self.input_dim = input_dim
        self.output_dim = output_dim
        self.selection_method = selection_method
        
        # Initialize appropriate selector
        if selection_method == 'attention':
            self.selector = AttentionBasedFeatureSelector(
                input_dim=input_dim,
                hidden_dim=hidden_dim,
                num_heads=4
            )
        elif selection_method == 'gating':
            self.selector = GatingBasedFeatureSelector(
                input_dim=input_dim,
                hidden_dim=hidden_dim,
                gate_type='sigmoid'
            )
        elif selection_method == 'l1':
            self.selector = L1RegularizedFeatureSelector(
                input_dim=input_dim,
                output_dim=output_dim,
                hidden_dims=[hidden_dim]
            )
        elif selection_method == 'learned':
            num_select = num_select or input_dim // 2
            self.selector = LearnedFeatureSelector(
                input_dim=input_dim,
                num_select=num_select,
                hidden_dim=hidden_dim
            )
        elif selection_method == 'importance':
            self.selector = ImportanceWeightingSelector(
                input_dim=input_dim,
                hidden_dim=hidden_dim,
                num_importance_heads=3
            )
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown selection method: {selection_method}")
        
        # Classifier head (not needed for L1 method which includes it)
        if selection_method != 'l1':
            self.classifier = nn.Sequential(
                nn.Linear(input_dim, hidden_dim),
                nn.ReLU(),
                nn.Dropout(0.1),
                nn.Linear(hidden_dim, output_dim)
            )
    
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Forward pass through selection and classification"""
        
        if self.selection_method == 'l1':
            # L1 method includes classification
            output = self.selector(x)
        else:
            # Other methods: select then classify
            selected_features, _ = self.selector(x)
            output = self.classifier(selected_features)
        
        return output
    
    def get_selection_loss(self) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Get additional selection loss (e.g., L1 regularization)"""
        
        if self.selection_method == 'l1':
            return self.selector.compute_l1_loss()
        return torch.tensor(0.0)


def comprehensive_example():
    """Comprehensive example comparing all feature selection methods"""
    
    print("="*70)
    print("COMPREHENSIVE FEATURE SELECTION COMPARISON")
    print("="*70)
    
    # Setup
    batch_size = 128
    num_features = 200
    output_dim = 10
    num_epochs = 20
    
    # Create synthetic dataset
    # Only first 50 features are relevant
    X_train = torch.randn(batch_size * 10, num_features)
    relevant_features = X_train[:, :50].sum(dim=1)
    y_train = (relevant_features > 0).long()
    
    X_test = torch.randn(batch_size * 2, num_features)
    relevant_features_test = X_test[:, :50].sum(dim=1)
    y_test = (relevant_features_test > 0).long()
    
    # Test each method
    methods = ['attention', 'gating', 'l1', 'learned', 'importance']
    results = {}
    
    for method in methods:
        print(f"\n{'='*70}")
        print(f"Testing {method.upper()} method")
        print(f"{'='*70}")
        
        # Initialize model
        if method == 'learned':
            model = FeatureSelectionPipeline(
                input_dim=num_features,
                output_dim=output_dim,
                selection_method=method,
                num_select=50,
                hidden_dim=64
            )
        else:
            model = FeatureSelectionPipeline(
                input_dim=num_features,
                output_dim=output_dim,
                selection_method=method,
                hidden_dim=64
            )
        
        # Training setup
        optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.001)
        criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
        
        # Training loop
        train_losses = []
        for epoch in range(num_epochs):
            model.train()
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            
            # Forward pass
            outputs = model(X_train)
            
            # Compute loss
            pred_loss = criterion(outputs, y_train)
            selection_loss = model.get_selection_loss()
            total_loss = pred_loss + selection_loss
            
            # Backward pass
            total_loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
            
            train_losses.append(total_loss.item())
            
            if (epoch + 1) % 5 == 0:
                print(f"Epoch {epoch+1}/{num_epochs} - Loss: {total_loss.item():.4f}")
        
        # Evaluation
        model.eval()
        with torch.no_grad():
            test_outputs = model(X_test)
            test_loss = criterion(test_outputs, y_test)
            test_acc = (test_outputs.argmax(dim=1) == y_test).float().mean()
        
        results[method] = {
            'final_train_loss': train_losses[-1],
            'test_loss': test_loss.item(),
            'test_accuracy': test_acc.item()
        }
        
        print(f"\nResults for {method}:")
        print(f"  Final Train Loss: {results[method]['final_train_loss']:.4f}")
        print(f"  Test Loss: {results[method]['test_loss']:.4f}")
        print(f"  Test Accuracy: {results[method]['test_accuracy']:.4f}")
    
    # Summary comparison
    print(f"\n{'='*70}")
    print("SUMMARY COMPARISON")
    print(f"{'='*70}")
    print(f"{'Method':<15} {'Train Loss':<15} {'Test Loss':<15} {'Test Acc':<15}")
    print(f"{'-'*70}")
    
    for method, result in results.items():
        print(f"{method:<15} {result['final_train_loss']:<15.4f} "
              f"{result['test_loss']:<15.4f} {result['test_accuracy']:<15.4f}")

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from typing import List, Dict

class FeatureSelectionVisualizer:
    """
    Utility class for visualizing feature selection results
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def plot_feature_importance(
        importance_scores: torch.Tensor,
        top_k: int = 20,
        title: str = "Feature Importance"
    ):
        """
        Plot feature importance scores
        
        Args:
            importance_scores: Tensor of importance scores
            top_k: Number of top features to display
            title: Plot title
        """
        # Convert to numpy
        scores = importance_scores.detach().cpu().numpy()
        
        # Get top-k features
        top_indices = np.argsort(scores)[-top_k:][::-1]
        top_scores = scores[top_indices]
        
        # Create plot
        plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
        plt.barh(range(top_k), top_scores)
        plt.yticks(range(top_k), [f"Feature {i}" for i in top_indices])
        plt.xlabel("Importance Score")
        plt.title(title)
        plt.gca().invert_yaxis()
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.show()
    
    @staticmethod
    def plot_selection_heatmap(
        selection_masks: torch.Tensor,
        sample_indices: List[int] = None,
        title: str = "Feature Selection Heatmap"
    ):
        """
        Plot heatmap of feature selections across samples
        
        Args:
            selection_masks: Tensor of selection masks (batch_size, num_features)
            sample_indices: Indices of samples to display
            title: Plot title
        """
        # Convert to numpy
        masks = selection_masks.detach().cpu().numpy()
        
        # Select samples
        if sample_indices is not None:
            masks = masks[sample_indices]
        
        # Create heatmap
        plt.figure(figsize=(14, 8))
        plt.imshow(masks, aspect='auto', cmap='YlOrRd', interpolation='nearest')
        plt.colorbar(label='Selection Weight')
        plt.xlabel('Feature Index')
        plt.ylabel('Sample Index')
        plt.title(title)
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.show()
    
    @staticmethod
    def plot_method_comparison(
        results: Dict[str, Dict[str, float]],
        metric: str = 'test_accuracy'
    ):
        """
        Plot comparison of different selection methods
        
        Args:
            results: Dictionary of results from different methods
            metric: Metric to compare
        """
        methods = list(results.keys())
        values = [results[m][metric] for m in methods]
        
        plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
        plt.bar(methods, values, color='steelblue', alpha=0.7)
        plt.xlabel('Selection Method')
        plt.ylabel(metric.replace('_', ' ').title())
        plt.title(f'Comparison of Feature Selection Methods - {metric}')
        plt.xticks(rotation=45)
        plt.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.show()
    
    @staticmethod
    def plot_training_curves(
        losses_dict: Dict[str, List[float]],
        title: str = "Training Curves"
    ):
        """
        Plot training curves for different methods
        
        Args:
            losses_dict: Dictionary mapping method names to loss lists
            title: Plot title
        """
        plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
        
        for method, losses in losses_dict.items():
            plt.plot(losses, label=method, linewidth=2)
        
        plt.xlabel('Epoch')
        plt.ylabel('Loss')
        plt.title(title)
        plt.legend()
        plt.grid(alpha=0.3)
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.show()


class FeatureSelectionEvaluator:
    """
    Utility class for evaluating feature selection quality
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def compute_selection_stability(
        selector: nn.Module,
        x: torch.Tensor,
        num_runs: int = 10
    ) -> float:
        """
        Compute stability of feature selection across multiple runs
        
        Args:
            selector: Feature selection model
            x: Input data
            num_runs: Number of runs for stability estimation
            
        Returns:
            Stability score (higher is more stable)
        """
        selector.eval()
        selections = []
        
        with torch.no_grad():
            for _ in range(num_runs):
                if hasattr(selector, 'get_selected_features'):
                    selected = selector.get_selected_features(x)
                elif hasattr(selector, 'get_feature_importance'):
                    importance = selector.get_feature_importance(x)
                    selected = torch.argsort(importance.mean(0), descending=True)
                else:
                    # Generic approach
                    _, mask = selector(x, return_selection=True) if hasattr(selector, 'forward') else (None, None)
                    if mask is not None:
                        selected = (mask > 0.5).float()
                    else:
                        return 0.0
                
                selections.append(selected)
        
        # Compute pairwise Jaccard similarity
        similarities = []
        for i in range(len(selections)):
            for j in range(i + 1, len(selections)):
                if selections[i].dim() == 2:
                    # Binary masks
                    intersection = (selections[i] * selections[j]).sum()
                    union = ((selections[i] + selections[j]) > 0).float().sum()
                else:
                    # Indices
                    set_i = set(selections[i].cpu().numpy().flatten())
                    set_j = set(selections[j].cpu().numpy().flatten())
                    intersection = len(set_i.intersection(set_j))
                    union = len(set_i.union(set_j))
                
                if union > 0:
                    similarities.append(intersection / union)
        
        return np.mean(similarities) if similarities else 0.0
    
    @staticmethod
    def compute_selection_sparsity(
        selection_mask: torch.Tensor,
        threshold: float = 0.01
    ) -> float:
        """
        Compute sparsity of feature selection
        
        Args:
            selection_mask: Selection mask tensor
            threshold: Threshold for considering a feature selected
            
        Returns:
            Sparsity ratio (0 = dense, 1 = completely sparse)
        """
        selected = (selection_mask > threshold).float()
        sparsity = 1.0 - (selected.sum() / selected.numel())
        return sparsity.item()
    
    @staticmethod
    def evaluate_selection_quality(
        selector: nn.Module,
        x: torch.Tensor,
        y: torch.Tensor,
        true_important_features: List[int] = None
    ) -> Dict[str, float]:
        """
        Comprehensive evaluation of feature selection quality
        
        Args:
            selector: Feature selection model
            x: Input data
            y: Target labels
            true_important_features: List of truly important feature indices
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary of evaluation metrics
        """
        metrics = {}
        
        # Stability
        metrics['stability'] = FeatureSelectionEvaluator.compute_selection_stability(
            selector, x, num_runs=5
        )
        
        # Get selection
        selector.eval()
        with torch.no_grad():
            if hasattr(selector, 'get_selected_features'):
                selected_indices = selector.get_selected_features(x)
                if selected_indices.dim() == 2:
                    selected_indices = selected_indices[0]  # Take first sample
            elif hasattr(selector, 'get_feature_importance'):
                importance = selector.get_feature_importance(x)
                selected_indices = torch.argsort(importance.mean(0), descending=True)
            else:
                selected_indices = None
        
        # Precision and recall (if ground truth available)
        if true_important_features is not None and selected_indices is not None:
            selected_set = set(selected_indices[:len(true_important_features)].cpu().numpy())
            true_set = set(true_important_features)
            
            intersection = len(selected_set.intersection(true_set))
            metrics['precision'] = intersection / len(selected_set) if selected_set else 0.0
            metrics['recall'] = intersection / len(true_set) if true_set else 0.0
            metrics['f1_score'] = (
                2 * metrics['precision'] * metrics['recall'] / 
                (metrics['precision'] + metrics['recall'])
                if (metrics['precision'] + metrics['recall']) > 0 else 0.0
            )
        
        return metrics


def advanced_example_with_evaluation():
    """
    Advanced example with comprehensive evaluation and visualization
    """
    print("\n" + "="*70)
    print("ADVANCED FEATURE SELECTION EXAMPLE WITH EVALUATION")
    print("="*70 + "\n")
    
    # Setup
    batch_size = 256
    num_features = 150
    num_important = 30
    output_dim = 5

    X[:, :num_important] *= 2.0

    y = (X[:, :num_important].sum(dim=1) > 0).long()
    true_important_features = list(range(num_important))
    
    # Test importance weighting method with evaluation
    print("Testing Importance Weighting with Comprehensive Evaluation\n")
    
    selector = ImportanceWeightingSelector(
        input_dim=num_features,
        hidden_dim=64,
        num_importance_heads=4,
        use_variance=True,
        use_gradient=False,
        dropout=0.1
    )
    
    # Training
    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(selector.parameters(), lr=0.001)
    num_epochs = 30
    
    print("Training...")
    for epoch in range(num_epochs):
        selector.train()
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        
        # Forward pass
        weighted_features, _ = selector(X)
        
        # Simple prediction based on weighted features
        predictions = weighted_features.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True)
        loss = F.mse_loss(predictions, y.float().unsqueeze(1))
        
        # Backward
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
        
        if (epoch + 1) % 10 == 0:
            print(f"Epoch {epoch+1}/{num_epochs} - Loss: {loss.item():.4f}")
    
    # Evaluation
    print("\n" + "-"*70)
    print("Evaluation Results")
    print("-"*70)
    
    evaluator = FeatureSelectionEvaluator()
    metrics = evaluator.evaluate_selection_quality(
        selector, X, y, true_important_features
    )
    
    print(f"Stability: {metrics['stability']:.4f}")
    if 'precision' in metrics:
        print(f"Precision: {metrics['precision']:.4f}")
        print(f"Recall: {metrics['recall']:.4f}")
        print(f"F1 Score: {metrics['f1_score']:.4f}")
    
    # Get feature importance and ranking
    importance_scores, ranked_indices = selector.get_feature_ranking(X)
    
    print(f"\nTop 10 Selected Features: {ranked_indices[:10].tolist()}")
    print(f"True Important Features: {true_important_features[:10]}")
    
    # Calculate overlap
    top_k = num_important
    selected_top_k = set(ranked_indices[:top_k].tolist())
    true_set = set(true_important_features)
    overlap = len(selected_top_k.intersection(true_set))
    
    print(f"\nOverlap with true important features: {overlap}/{num_important}")
    print(f"Overlap percentage: {100 * overlap / num_important:.2f}%")
    
    # Sparsity analysis
    _, importance_weights = selector(X, return_importance=True)
    sparsity = evaluator.compute_selection_sparsity(importance_weights, threshold=0.5)
    print(f"Selection sparsity: {sparsity:.4f}")
    
    print("\n" + "="*70)


# Performance benchmarking utility
class FeatureSelectionBenchmark:
    """
    Benchmark different feature selection methods
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def benchmark_inference_time(
        selector: nn.Module,
        input_shape: tuple,
        num_iterations: int = 100,
        device: str = 'cpu'
    ) -> Dict[str, float]:
        """
        Benchmark inference time
        
        Args:
            selector: Feature selection model
            input_shape: Shape of input tensor
            num_iterations: Number of iterations for timing
            device: Device to run on
            
        Returns:
            Timing statistics
        """
        import time
        
        selector = selector.to(device)
        selector.eval()
        
        # Warmup
        x = torch.randn(*input_shape, device=device)
        with torch.no_grad():
            for _ in range(10):
                _ = selector(x)
        
        # Benchmark
        times = []
        with torch.no_grad():
            for _ in range(num_iterations):
                x = torch.randn(*input_shape, device=device)
                
                start = time.time()
                _ = selector(x)
                end = time.time()
                
                times.append(end - start)
        
        return {
            'mean_time': np.mean(times),
            'std_time': np.std(times),
            'min_time': np.min(times),
            'max_time': np.max(times)
        }
    
    @staticmethod
    def benchmark_memory_usage(
        selector: nn.Module,
        input_shape: tuple
    ) -> Dict[str, int]:
        """
        Benchmark memory usage
        
        Args:
            selector: Feature selection model
            input_shape: Shape of input tensor
            
        Returns:
            Memory statistics
        """
        # Count parameters
        total_params = sum(p.numel() for p in selector.parameters())
        trainable_params =
```python
        trainable_params = sum(p.numel() for p in selector.parameters() if p.requires_grad)
        
        # Estimate memory (4 bytes per float32 parameter)
        param_memory = total_params * 4 / (1024 ** 2)  # MB
        
        return {
            'total_parameters': total_params,
            'trainable_parameters': trainable_params,
            'parameter_memory_mb': param_memory
        }
