# Example 21: Scaling pattern cheat sheet
def print_scaling_cheat_sheet():
    """Print a comprehensive cheat sheet for all scaling patterns."""
    
    cheat_sheet = """
╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║                      MODEL SCALING PATTERNS CHEAT SHEET                      ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 1. WIDTH SCALING                                                             │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Code Example:
    model = WidthScalableNet(width_multiplier=1.5)
  
  When to Use:
    ✓ Need quick capacity increase
    ✓ Shallow network architectures
    ✓ Limited by depth constraints
  
  Multiplier Guide:
    • 0.5x  → Mobile/Tiny models
    • 0.75x → Small models
    • 1.0x  → Base model
    • 1.5x  → Large models
    • 2.0x  → Extra large models
  
  Tips:
    • Keep channels divisible by 8
    • Use batch normalization
    • Monitor parameter count

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 2. DEPTH SCALING                                                             │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Code Example:
    model = DepthScalableNet(depth_multiplier=2.0)
  
  When to Use:
    ✓ Complex hierarchical features needed
    ✓ Sufficient training data available
    ✓ Can afford longer training time
  
  Multiplier Guide:
    • 0.5x  → Shallow (faster)
    • 1.0x  → Base depth
    • 1.5x  → Deep
    • 2.0x  → Very deep (use residuals!)
  
  Tips:
    • Always use skip connections
    • Apply gradient clipping
    • Use learning rate warmup
    • Monitor gradient flow

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 3. RESOLUTION SCALING                                                        │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Code Example:
    model = ResolutionScalableNet(base_resolution=224)
    input = torch.randn(1, 3, 384, 384)  # Higher resolution
  
  When to Use:
    ✓ Fine-grained details important
    ✓ Large objects in images
    ✓ Medical/satellite imagery
  
  Resolution Guide:
    • 128x128  → Tiny/Mobile
    • 224x224  → Standard
    • 384x384  → High detail
    • 512x512+ → Very high detail
  
  Tips:
    • Use progressive resolution training
    • Adjust batch size accordingly
    • Consider memory constraints
    • Use adaptive pooling

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 4. COMPOUND SCALING                                                          │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Code Example:
    model = CompoundScalableNet(compound_coef=2)
  
  When to Use:
    ✓ Building model families
    ✓ Need balanced scaling
    ✓ Following EfficientNet approach
  
  Coefficient Guide (φ):
    • φ=0 → B0 (base)
    • φ=1 → B1 (small)
    • φ=2 → B2 (medium)
    • φ=3 → B3 (large)
    • φ=4+ → B4+ (very large)
  
  Scaling Rules:
    • depth = α^φ    (α ≈ 1.2)
    • width = β^φ    (β ≈ 1.1)
    • resolution = γ^φ (γ ≈ 1.15)
  
  Tips:
    • Start with proven coefficients
    • Grid search for custom α,β,γ
    • Validate on target dataset

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 5. EFFICIENT SCALING                                                         │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Code Example:
    model = EfficientScalableNet(
        width_multiplier=1.0,
        depth_multiplier=1.0
    )
  
  When to Use:
    ✓ Mobile/edge deployment
    ✓ Strict latency requirements
    ✓ Limited computational resources
  
  Configuration Guide:
    • Tiny:   width=0.5,  depth=0.5
    • Small:  width=0.75, depth=0.75
    • Base:   width=1.0,  depth=1.0
    • Large:  width=1.5,  depth=1.5
  
  Key Features:
    • Depthwise separable convolutions
    • Inverted residuals
    • Squeeze-and-excitation
    • Linear bottlenecks
  
  Tips:
    • Profile on target hardware
    • Use knowledge distillation
    • Apply quantization
    • Optimize for specific backend

    📱 Mobile (< 5M params)    → Efficient Scaling (0.5x-0.75x)
    🖥️  Edge (5-10M params)    → Efficient Scaling (1.0x)
    ☁️  Server (10-50M params) → Compound Scaling (φ=1-3)
    🔬 Research (> 50M params) → Compound Scaling (φ=3+)

  Primary Goal:

    ⚡ Min Latency      → Efficient Scaling (small multipliers)

    📈 Moderate  → Compound Scaling (φ=1)
    📉 Complex   → Compound Scaling (φ=2-3)
    📊 Very Hard → Compound Scaling (φ=3+) + Ensemble

)

    base_resolution=128,
    target_resolution=384,
    num_stages=3
)

    # Train at this resolution...


Example 6: Knowledge distillation
---------------------------------
from scaling_patterns import (
    EfficientScalableNet,
    KnowledgeDistillationLoss
)

# Teacher (large model)
teacher = EfficientScalableNet(width_multiplier=2.0, depth_multiplier=2.0)
teacher.load_state_dict(torch.load('teacher_weights.pth'))
teacher.eval()

# Student (small model)
student = EfficientScalableNet(width_multiplier=0.5, depth_multiplier=0.5)

# Distillation loss
kd_loss = KnowledgeDistillationLoss(temperature=4.0, alpha=0.7)

# Training loop
for inputs, targets in train_loader:
    with torch.no_grad():
        teacher_logits = teacher(inputs)
    
    student_logits = student(inputs)
    loss, hard_loss, soft_loss = kd_loss(
        student_logits, teacher_logits, targets
    )
    
    # Backprop and optimize...

# PyTorch Sparsity Induction Patterns
# Complete implementation of 6 sparsity patterns for neural network compression

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F
import numpy as np
from typing import Optional, List, Tuple
import copy

# ============================================================================
# 1. L1 Sparsity Pattern
# ============================================================================

class L1SparsityPattern(nn.Module):
    """
    L1 Sparsity Pattern - Encourages sparsity through L1 regularization.
    Adds L1 penalty to the loss function to push small weights toward zero.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, model: nn.Module, lambda_l1: float = 1e-4):
        """
        Args:
            model: Neural network model to apply sparsity
            lambda_l1: L1 regularization coefficient
        """
        super().__init__()
        self.model = model
        self.lambda_l1 = lambda_l1
        
    def forward(self, x):
        return self.model(x)
    
    def compute_l1_loss(self) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Compute L1 regularization loss across all parameters."""
        l1_loss = 0.0
        for param in self.model.parameters():
            if param.requires_grad:
                l1_loss += torch.sum(torch.abs(param))
        return self.lambda_l1 * l1_loss
    
    def get_sparsity(self) -> float:
        """Calculate the percentage of zero weights."""
        total_params = 0
        zero_params = 0
        for param in self.model.parameters():
            total_params += param.numel()
            zero_params += torch.sum(param == 0).item()
        return 100.0 * zero_params / total_params
    
    def apply_threshold(self, threshold: float = 1e-3):
        """Zero out weights below threshold."""
        with torch.no_grad():
            for param in self.model.parameters():
                param.data[torch.abs(param.data) < threshold] = 0


# ============================================================================
# 2. Group Sparsity Pattern
# ============================================================================

class GroupSparsityPattern(nn.Module):
    """
    Group Sparsity Pattern - Encourages entire groups of weights to be zero.
    Useful for structured pruning of filters, channels, or attention heads.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, model: nn.Module, lambda_group: float = 1e-3, 
                 group_size: int = 4):
        """
        Args:
            model: Neural network model
            lambda_group: Group sparsity regularization coefficient
            group_size: Size of each group
        """
        super().__init__()
        self.model = model
        self.lambda_group = lambda_group
        self.group_size = group_size
        
    def forward(self, x):
        return self.model(x)
    
    def compute_group_lasso_loss(self) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Compute group lasso (L2,1 norm) loss.
        Groups weights and applies L2 norm within groups, L1 norm across groups.
        """
        group_loss = 0.0
        
        for name, param in self.model.named_parameters():
            if param.requires_grad and len(param.shape) >= 2:
                # Reshape parameter into groups
                flat_param = param.view(-1)
                n_groups = flat_param.shape[0] // self.group_size
                
                if n_groups > 0:
                    # Reshape into groups and compute L2 norm per group
                    groups = flat_param[:n_groups * self.group_size].view(
                        n_groups, self.group_size
                    )
                    # L2 norm within groups, then L1 norm across groups
                    group_norms = torch.norm(groups, p=2, dim=1)
                    group_loss += torch.sum(group_norms)
        
        return self.lambda_group * group_loss
    
    def prune_groups(self, threshold: float = 0.1):
        """Prune entire groups with small L2 norms."""
        with torch.no_grad():
            for param in self.model.parameters():
                if len(param.shape) >= 2:
                    flat_param = param.view(-1)
                    n_groups = flat_param.shape[0] // self.group_size
                    
                    if n_groups > 0:
                        groups = flat_param[:n_groups * self.group_size].view(
                            n_groups, self.group_size
                        )
                        group_norms = torch.norm(groups, p=2, dim=1)
                        
                        # Zero out groups below threshold
                        mask = group_norms < threshold
                        groups[mask] = 0
                        flat_param[:n_groups * self.group_size] = groups.view(-1)


# ============================================================================
# 3. Structured Sparsity Pattern
# ============================================================================

class StructuredSparsityPattern(nn.Module):
    """
    Structured Sparsity Pattern - Prunes entire structures like filters,
    channels, or rows/columns to maintain efficient computation.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, model: nn.Module, structure_type: str = 'filter'):
        """
        Args:
            model: Neural network model
            structure_type: Type of structure ('filter', 'channel', 'row', 'column')
        """
        super().__init__()
        self.model = model
        self.structure_type = structure_type
        self.masks = {}
        self._initialize_masks()
        
    def _initialize_masks(self):
        """Initialize binary masks for each parameter."""
        for name, param in self.model.named_parameters():
            if param.requires_grad:
                self.masks[name] = torch.ones_like(param)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        # Apply masks during forward pass
        self._apply_masks()
        return self.model(x)
    
    def _apply_masks(self):
        """Apply stored masks to model parameters."""
        with torch.no_grad():
            for name, param in self.model.named_parameters():
                if name in self.masks:
                    param.data *= self.masks[name]
    
    def prune_structures(self, sparsity_ratio: float = 0.5):
        """
        Prune structures based on their importance (L2 norm).
        
        Args:
            sparsity_ratio: Fraction of structures to prune (0 to 1)
        """
        for name, param in self.model.named_parameters():
            if not param.requires_grad or len(param.shape) < 2:
                continue
            
            if self.structure_type == 'filter' and len(param.shape) == 4:
                # For Conv2d weights [out_channels, in_channels, H, W]
                importance = torch.norm(param.view(param.shape[0], -1), p=2, dim=1)
                n_prune = int(sparsity_ratio * param.shape[0])
                threshold = torch.kthvalue(importance, n_prune + 1)[0]
                
                mask = importance > threshold
                self.masks[name] = mask.view(-1, 1, 1, 1).expand_as(param).float()
                
            elif self.structure_type == 'channel' and len(param.shape) == 4:
                # Prune input channels
                importance = torch.norm(param.view(param.shape[0], param.shape[1], -1), 
                                       p=2, dim=(0, 2))
                n_prune = int(sparsity_ratio * param.shape[1])
                threshold = torch.kthvalue(importance, n_prune + 1)[0]
                
                mask = importance > threshold
                self.masks[name] = mask.view(1, -1, 1, 1).expand_as(param).float()
                
            elif self.structure_type == 'row':
                # Prune rows (output neurons)
                importance = torch.norm(param, p=2, dim=1)
                n_prune = int(sparsity_ratio * param.shape[0])
                threshold = torch.kthvalue(importance, n_prune + 1)[0]
                
                mask = importance > threshold
                self.masks[name] = mask.view(-1, 1).expand_as(param).float()
    
    def get_structure_sparsity(self) -> dict:
        """Get sparsity statistics for each layer."""
        stats = {}
        for name, mask in self.masks.items():
            if self.structure_type in ['filter', 'row']:
                # Count zero structures along dimension 0
                zero_structures = (mask.view(mask.shape[0], -1).sum(dim=1) == 0).sum()
                total_structures = mask.shape[0]
            else:
                zero_structures = (mask.sum() == 0).sum()
                total_structures = mask.numel()
            
            stats[name] = {
                'zero_structures': zero_structures.item(),
                'total_structures': total_structures,
                'sparsity': 100.0 * zero_structures.item() / total_structures
            }
        return stats


# ============================================================================
# 4. Learned Sparsity Pattern
# ============================================================================

class LearnedSparsityPattern(nn.Module):
    """
    Learned Sparsity Pattern - Uses learnable binary masks (Gumbel-Softmax)
    to automatically learn which weights to keep or prune.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, model: nn.Module, temperature: float = 1.0, 
                 target_sparsity: float = 0.5):
        """
        Args:
            model: Neural network model
            temperature: Gumbel-Softmax temperature (lower = more discrete)
            target_sparsity: Target sparsity level for regularization
        """
        super().__init__()
        self.model = model
        self.temperature = temperature
        self.target_sparsity = target_sparsity
        
        # Create learnable mask parameters
        self.mask_params = nn.ParameterDict()
        for name, param in model.named_parameters():
            if param.requires_grad:
                # Initialize mask logits (before sigmoid/gumbel)
                self.mask_params[name.replace('.', '_')] = nn.Parameter(
                    torch.ones_like(param) * 2.0  # Start with high probability of keeping
                )
    
    def forward(self, x):
        # Apply learned masks
        self._apply_learned_masks()
        return self.model(x)
    
    def _apply_learned_masks(self):
        """Apply learned stochastic masks using Gumbel-Softmax."""
        for (name, param), (mask_name, mask_logits) in zip(
            self.model.named_parameters(), self.mask_params.items()
        ):
            if param.requires_grad:
                if self.training:
                    # Gumbel-Softmax for differentiable sampling
                    mask = self._gumbel_sigmoid(mask_logits, self.temperature)
                else:
                    # Hard mask during inference
                    mask = (torch.sigmoid(mask_logits) > 0.5).float()
                
                param.data = param.data * mask
    
    def _gumbel_sigmoid(self, logits: torch.Tensor, temperature: float) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Gumbel-Softmax trick for binary masks.
        Provides differentiable approximation to sampling.
        """
        # Sample from Gumbel(0, 1)
        gumbel_noise = -torch.log(-torch.log(torch.rand_like(logits) + 1e-8) + 1e-8)
        # Apply Gumbel-Softmax
        y = torch.sigmoid((logits + gumbel_noise) / temperature)
        return y
    
    def compute_sparsity_loss(self) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Regularization loss to encourage target sparsity.
        Uses KL divergence between current and target sparsity.
        """
        total_params = 0
        expected_zeros = 0
        
        for mask_logits in self.mask_params.values():
            probs = torch.sigmoid(mask_logits)
            total_params += probs.numel()
            expected_zeros += torch.sum(1 - probs)  # Expected number of zeros
        
        current_sparsity = expected_zeros / total_params
        # L2 loss to target sparsity
        sparsity_loss = (current_sparsity - self.target_sparsity) ** 2
        
        return sparsity_loss
    
    def get_hard_masks(self) -> dict:
        """Get binarized masks for inference."""
        hard_masks = {}
        for name, mask_logits in self.mask_params.items():
            hard_masks[name] = (torch.sigmoid(mask_logits) > 0.5).float()
        return hard_masks


# ============================================================================
# 5. Magnitude Pruning Pattern
# ============================================================================

class MagnitudePruningPattern(nn.Module):
    """
    Magnitude Pruning Pattern - Prunes weights with smallest absolute values.
    Classic and effective pruning method based on weight magnitude.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, model: nn.Module, initial_sparsity: float = 0.0,
                 final_sparsity: float = 0.9, pruning_schedule: str = 'polynomial'):
        """
        Args:
            model: Neural network model
            initial_sparsity: Starting sparsity level
            final_sparsity: Target sparsity level
            pruning_schedule: 'polynomial', 'exponential', or 'linear'
        """
        super().__init__()
        self.model = model
        self.initial_sparsity = initial_sparsity
        self.final_sparsity = final_sparsity
        self.pruning_schedule = pruning_schedule
        self.current_step = 0
        self.masks = {}
        
        # Initialize masks
        for name, param in model.named_parameters():
            if param.requires_grad:
                self.masks[name] = torch.ones_like(param)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        self._apply_masks()
        return self.model(x)
    
    def _apply_masks(self):
        """Apply pruning masks to model parameters."""
        with torch.no_grad():
            for name, param in self.model.named_parameters():
                if name in self.masks:
                    param.data *= self.masks[name]
    
    def compute_sparsity_schedule(self, step: int, total_steps: int) -> float:
        """
        Compute current target sparsity based on schedule.
        
        Args:
            step: Current training step
            total_steps: Total number of pruning steps
        """
        if step >= total_steps:
            return self.final_sparsity
        
        progress = step / total_steps
        
        if self.pruning_schedule == 'polynomial':
            # Polynomial decay (cubic by default)
            current_sparsity = self.final_sparsity + (
                self.initial_sparsity - self.final_sparsity
            ) * (1 - progress) ** 3
            
        elif self.pruning_schedule == 'exponential':
            # Exponential decay
            current_sparsity = self.final_sparsity + (
                self.initial_sparsity - self.final_
final_sparsity
            ) * np.exp(-5 * progress)
            
        else:  # linear
            current_sparsity = (
                self.initial_sparsity + 
                (self.final_sparsity - self.initial_sparsity) * progress
            )
        
        return current_sparsity
    
    def prune_by_magnitude(self, sparsity: float):
        """
        Prune weights with smallest magnitudes globally or per-layer.
        
        Args:
            sparsity: Target sparsity ratio (0 to 1)
        """
        with torch.no_grad():
            # Global magnitude pruning
            all_weights = []
            for name, param in self.model.named_parameters():
                if param.requires_grad and name in self.masks:
                    all_weights.append(param.abs().view(-1))
            
            # Concatenate all weights and find threshold
            all_weights = torch.cat(all_weights)
            n_prune = int(sparsity * all_weights.numel())
            
            if n_prune > 0:
                threshold = torch.kthvalue(all_weights, n_prune)[0]
                
                # Apply threshold to create masks
                for name, param in self.model.named_parameters():
                    if param.requires_grad and name in self.masks:
                        self.masks[name] = (param.abs() > threshold).float()
    
    def prune_by_magnitude_layerwise(self, sparsity: float):
        """
        Prune weights with smallest magnitudes per layer.
        
        Args:
            sparsity: Target sparsity ratio per layer
        """
        with torch.no_grad():
            for name, param in self.model.named_parameters():
                if param.requires_grad and name in self.masks:
                    flat_param = param.abs().view(-1)
                    n_prune = int(sparsity * flat_param.numel())
                    
                    if n_prune > 0:
                        threshold = torch.kthvalue(flat_param, n_prune)[0]
                        self.masks[name] = (param.abs() > threshold).float()
    
    def step_pruning(self, current_step: int, total_steps: int, 
                     layerwise: bool = False):
        """
        Perform one step of iterative magnitude pruning.
        
        Args:
            current_step: Current training step
            total_steps: Total pruning steps
            layerwise: Whether to prune per-layer or globally
        """
        self.current_step = current_step
        target_sparsity = self.compute_sparsity_schedule(current_step, total_steps)
        
        if layerwise:
            self.prune_by_magnitude_layerwise(target_sparsity)
        else:
            self.prune_by_magnitude(target_sparsity)
    
    def get_sparsity_stats(self) -> dict:
        """Get detailed sparsity statistics."""
        stats = {
            'overall': {'total': 0, 'zero': 0},
            'per_layer': {}
        }
        
        for name, mask in self.masks.items():
            total = mask.numel()
            zero = (mask == 0).sum().item()
            
            stats['overall']['total'] += total
            stats['overall']['zero'] += zero
            stats['per_layer'][name] = {
                'total': total,
                'zero': zero,
                'sparsity': 100.0 * zero / total
            }
        
        stats['overall']['sparsity'] = (
            100.0 * stats['overall']['zero'] / stats['overall']['total']
        )
        
        return stats


# ============================================================================
# 6. Movement Pruning Pattern
# ============================================================================

class MovementPruningPattern(nn.Module):
    """
    Movement Pruning Pattern - Prunes weights based on their movement during
    training rather than just magnitude. Considers both magnitude and gradient
    information to determine importance.
    
    Reference: "Movement Pruning: Adaptive Sparsity by Fine-Tuning" (Sanh et al., 2020)
    """
    
    def __init__(self, model: nn.Module, initial_sparsity: float = 0.0,
                 final_sparsity: float = 0.9, initial_warmup: int = 0):
        """
        Args:
            model: Neural network model
            initial_sparsity: Starting sparsity level
            final_sparsity: Target sparsity level
            initial_warmup: Number of steps before starting pruning
        """
        super().__init__()
        self.model = model
        self.initial_sparsity = initial_sparsity
        self.final_sparsity = final_sparsity
        self.initial_warmup = initial_warmup
        self.current_step = 0
        
        # Store masks and importance scores
        self.masks = {}
        self.importance_scores = {}
        self.weight_momentum = {}
        
        # Initialize tracking structures
        for name, param in model.named_parameters():
            if param.requires_grad:
                self.masks[name] = torch.ones_like(param)
                self.importance_scores[name] = torch.zeros_like(param)
                self.weight_momentum[name] = torch.zeros_like(param)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        self._apply_masks()
        return self.model(x)
    
    def _apply_masks(self):
        """Apply pruning masks to model parameters."""
        with torch.no_grad():
            for name, param in self.model.named_parameters():
                if name in self.masks:
                    param.data *= self.masks[name]
    
    def compute_importance_scores(self, momentum: float = 0.9):
        """
        Compute importance scores based on movement.
        Movement = weight * gradient (direction of weight update)
        
        Args:
            momentum: Momentum factor for smoothing importance scores
        """
        with torch.no_grad():
            for name, param in self.model.named_parameters():
                if param.requires_grad and name in self.importance_scores:
                    if param.grad is not None:
                        # Movement score: weight magnitude * gradient direction
                        # Positive movement means weight is moving away from zero
                        movement = -param.data * param.grad.data
                        
                        # Update importance with momentum
                        self.importance_scores[name] = (
                            momentum * self.importance_scores[name] + 
                            (1 - momentum) * movement
                        )
    
    def prune_by_movement(self, sparsity: float):
        """
        Prune weights based on movement scores.
        Weights moving toward zero are more likely to be pruned.
        
        Args:
            sparsity: Target sparsity ratio
        """
        with torch.no_grad():
            # Collect all importance scores
            all_scores = []
            for name in self.importance_scores:
                all_scores.append(self.importance_scores[name].view(-1))
            
            all_scores = torch.cat(all_scores)
            n_prune = int(sparsity * all_scores.numel())
            
            if n_prune > 0:
                # Prune weights with lowest importance (most negative movement)
                threshold = torch.kthvalue(all_scores, n_prune)[0]
                
                # Update masks
                for name in self.importance_scores:
                    self.masks[name] = (
                        self.importance_scores[name] > threshold
                    ).float()
    
    def prune_by_movement_layerwise(self, sparsity: float):
        """
        Prune weights based on movement scores per layer.
        
        Args:
            sparsity: Target sparsity ratio per layer
        """
        with torch.no_grad():
            for name, scores in self.importance_scores.items():
                flat_scores = scores.view(-1)
                n_prune = int(sparsity * flat_scores.numel())
                
                if n_prune > 0:
                    threshold = torch.kthvalue(flat_scores, n_prune)[0]
                    self.masks[name] = (scores > threshold).float()
    
    def step_pruning(self, current_step: int, total_steps: int,
                     momentum: float = 0.9, layerwise: bool = False):
        """
        Perform one step of movement pruning.
        
        Args:
            current_step: Current training step
            total_steps: Total pruning steps
            momentum: Momentum for importance score smoothing
            layerwise: Whether to prune per-layer or globally
        """
        self.current_step = current_step
        
        # Skip pruning during warmup
        if current_step < self.initial_warmup:
            return
        
        # Compute importance scores from gradients
        self.compute_importance_scores(momentum)
        
        # Compute target sparsity with polynomial schedule
        adjusted_step = current_step - self.initial_warmup
        adjusted_total = total_steps - self.initial_warmup
        
        if adjusted_step >= adjusted_total:
            target_sparsity = self.final_sparsity
        else:
            progress = adjusted_step / adjusted_total
            target_sparsity = self.final_sparsity + (
                self.initial_sparsity - self.final_sparsity
            ) * (1 - progress) ** 3
        
        # Prune based on movement
        if layerwise:
            self.prune_by_movement_layerwise(target_sparsity)
        else:
            self.prune_by_movement(target_sparsity)
    
    def get_movement_stats(self) -> dict:
        """Get statistics about weight movements."""
        stats = {}
        
        for name, scores in self.importance_scores.items():
            stats[name] = {
                'mean_movement': scores.mean().item(),
                'std_movement': scores.std().item(),
                'positive_movement': (scores > 0).sum().item(),
                'negative_movement': (scores < 0).sum().item(),
                'sparsity': 100.0 * (self.masks[name] == 0).sum().item() / self.masks[name].numel()
            }
        
        return stats
    
    def get_sparsity(self) -> float:
        """Get overall sparsity percentage."""
        total = 0
        zero = 0
        for mask in self.masks.values():
            total += mask.numel()
            zero += (mask == 0).sum().item()
        return 100.0 * zero / total

def create_sample_model():
    """Create a simple model for demonstration."""
    return nn.Sequential(
        nn.Linear(784, 256),
        nn.ReLU(),
        nn.Linear(256, 128),
        nn.ReLU(),
        nn.Linear(128, 10)
    )


def demonstrate_l1_sparsity():
    """Demonstrate L1 Sparsity Pattern."""
    print("=" * 80)
    print("1. L1 SPARSITY PATTERN DEMONSTRATION")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    model = create_sample_model()
    l1_sparse = L1SparsityPattern(model, lambda_l1=1e-4)
    
    # Dummy data
    x = torch.randn(32, 784)
    y = torch.randint(0, 10, (32,))
    
    # Training loop
    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(l1_sparse.parameters(), lr=0.001)
    criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
    
    print(f"Initial sparsity: {l1_sparse.get_sparsity():.2f}%")
    
    for epoch in range(5):
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        output = l1_sparse(x)
        ce_loss = criterion(output, y)
        l1_loss = l1_sparse.compute_l1_loss()
        total_loss = ce_loss + l1_loss
        
        total_loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
        
        print(f"Epoch {epoch+1}: CE Loss = {ce_loss.item():.4f}, "
              f"L1 Loss = {l1_loss.item():.4f}")
    
    # Apply threshold to enforce sparsity
    l1_sparse.apply_threshold(threshold=0.01)
    print(f"Final sparsity after thresholding: {l1_sparse.get_sparsity():.2f}%\n")


def demonstrate_group_sparsity():
    """Demonstrate Group Sparsity Pattern."""
    print("=" * 80)
    print("2. GROUP SPARSITY PATTERN DEMONSTRATION")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    model = create_sample_model()
    group_sparse = GroupSparsityPattern(model, lambda_group=1e-3, group_size=4)
    
    # Dummy data
    x = torch.randn(32, 784)
    y = torch.randint(0, 10, (32,))
    
    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(group_sparse.parameters(), lr=0.001)
    criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
    
    for epoch in range(5):
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        output = group_sparse(x)
        ce_loss = criterion(output, y)
        group_loss = group_sparse.compute_group_lasso_loss()
        total_loss = ce_loss + group_loss
        
        total_loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
        
        print(f"Epoch {epoch+1}: CE Loss = {ce_loss.item():.4f}, "
              f"Group Loss = {group_loss.item():.4f}")
    
    # Prune groups
    group_sparse.prune_groups(threshold=0.5)
    print("Groups pruned with threshold 0.5\n")

        # Training step
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        output = movement_pruning(x)
        loss = criterion(output, y)
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
        
        # Movement pruning step (uses gradients)
        movement_pruning.step_pruning(
            step, total_steps, momentum=0.9, layerwise=False
        )
        
        if step % 5 == 0:
            sparsity = movement_pruning.get_sparsity()
            print(f"Step {step}: Loss = {loss.item():.4f}, "
                  f"Sparsity = {sparsity:.2f}%")
    
    # Movement statistics
    print("\nMovement statistics per layer:")
    movement_stats = movement_pruning.get_movement_stats()
    for layer_name, stats in movement_stats.items():
        print(f"  {layer_name}:")
        print(f"    Mean movement: {stats['mean_movement']:.6f}")
        print(f"    Positive/Negative: {stats['positive_movement']}/{stats['negative_movement']}")
        print(f"    Sparsity: {stats['sparsity']:.2f}%")
    print()


def compare_all_patterns():
    """Compare all sparsity patterns side by side."""
    print("=" * 80)
    print("COMPARISON OF ALL SPARSITY PATTERNS")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Create identical models for fair comparison
    models = {
        'L1': create_sample_model(),
        'Group': create_sample_model(),
        'Magnitude': create_sample_model(),
        'Movement': create_sample_model(),
    }
    
    # Initialize patterns
    patterns = {
        'L1': L1SparsityPattern(models['L1'], lambda_l1=1e-3),
        'Group': GroupSparsityPattern(models['Group'], lambda_group=1e-2, group_size=4),
        'Magnitude': MagnitudePruningPattern(models['Magnitude'], 
                                             initial_sparsity=0.0, 
                                             final_sparsity=0.8),
        'Movement': MovementPruningPattern(models['Movement'], 
                                          initial_sparsity=0.0, 
                                          final_sparsity=0.8,
                                          initial_warmup=3),
    }
    
    # Create optimizers
    optimizers = {
        name: torch.optim.Adam(pattern.parameters() if hasattr(pattern, 'parameters') 
                               else pattern.model.parameters(), lr=0.001)
        for name, pattern in patterns.items()
    }
    
    criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
    
    # Dummy data
    x = torch.randn(32, 784)
    y = torch.randint(0, 10, (32,))
    
    total_steps = 15
    
    print(f"Training for {total_steps} steps...\n")
    
    for step in range(total_steps):
        for name, pattern in patterns.items():
            optimizer = optimizers[name]
            
            # Forward pass
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            output = pattern(x)
            ce_loss = criterion(output, y)
            
            # Add regularization losses where applicable
            total_loss = ce_loss
            if name == 'L1':
                total_loss = ce_loss + pattern.compute_l1_loss()
            elif name == 'Group':
                total_loss = ce_loss + pattern.compute_group_lasso_loss()
            
            # Backward pass
            total_loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
            
            # Apply pruning
            if name == 'Magnitude':
                pattern.step_pruning(step, total_steps, layerwise=False)
            elif name == 'Movement':
                pattern.step_pruning(step, total_steps, momentum=0.9, layerwise=False)
    
    # Final pruning for non-iterative methods
    patterns['L1'].apply_threshold(threshold=0.01)
    patterns['Group'].prune_groups(threshold=0.3)
    
    # Compare results
    print("Final Results:")
    print("-" * 80)
    print(f"{'Pattern':<15} {'Sparsity':<15} {'Loss':<15}")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    for name, pattern in patterns.items():
        # Compute sparsity
        if name == 'L1':
            sparsity = pattern.get_sparsity()
        elif name == 'Magnitude' or name == 'Movement':
            sparsity = pattern.get_sparsity()
        else:  # Group
            total = sum(p.numel() for p in pattern.model.parameters())
            zeros = sum((p == 0).sum().item() for p in pattern.model.parameters())
            sparsity = 100.0 * zeros / total
        
        # Compute final loss
        with torch.no_grad():
            output = pattern(x)
            final_loss = criterion(output, y).item()
        
        print(f"{name:<15} {sparsity:>6.2f}%{'':<8} {final_loss:>6.4f}")
    
    print("-" * 80)
    print()


def advanced_example_with_real_training():
    """Advanced example showing integration with real training loop."""
    print("=" * 80)
    print("ADVANCED EXAMPLE: MOVEMENT PRUNING WITH TRAINING LOOP")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Create a slightly larger model
    class SimpleNet(nn.Module):
        def __init__(self):
            super().__init__()
            self.fc1 = nn.Linear(784, 512)
            self.bn1 = nn.BatchNorm1d(512)
            self.fc2 = nn.Linear(512, 256)
            self.bn2 = nn.BatchNorm1d(256)
            self.fc3 = nn.Linear(256, 10)
            self.dropout = nn.Dropout(0.2)
        
        def forward(self, x):
            x = F.relu(self.bn1(self.fc1(x)))
            x = self.dropout(x)
            x = F.relu(self.bn2(self.fc2(x)))
            x = self.dropout(x)
            x = self.fc3(x)
            return x
    
    model = SimpleNet()
    
    # Apply movement pruning
    pruned_model = MovementPruningPattern(
        model,
        initial_sparsity=0.0,
        final_sparsity=0.85,
        initial_warmup=10
    )
    
    # Training setup
    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(pruned_model.model.parameters(), lr=0.001)
    scheduler = torch.optim.lr_scheduler.CosineAnnealingLR(optimizer, T_max=50)
    criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
    
    # Simulate training data
    num_epochs = 5
    steps_per_epoch = 10
    total_steps = num_epochs * steps_per_epoch
    
    print(f"Training for {num_epochs} epochs, {steps_per_epoch} steps each")
    print(f"Total pruning steps: {total_steps}")
    print(f"Warmup: {pruned_model.initial_warmup} steps")
    print()
    
    global_step = 0
    
    for epoch in range(num_epochs):
        epoch_loss = 0.0
        
        for step in range(steps_per_epoch):
            # Simulate batch
            x = torch.randn(64, 784)
            y = torch.randint(0, 10, (64,))
            
            # Training step
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            output = pruned_model(x)
            loss = criterion(output, y)
            loss.backward()
            
            # Gradient clipping
            torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(pruned_model.model.parameters(), 1.0)
            
            optimizer.step()
            
            # Movement pruning step
            pruned_model.step_pruning(global_step, total_steps, momentum=0.95)
            
            epoch_loss += loss.item()
            global_step += 1
        
        scheduler.step()
        
        # Epoch summary
        avg_loss = epoch_loss / steps_per_epoch
        sparsity = pruned_model.get_sparsity()
        lr = optimizer.param_groups[0]['lr']
        
        print(f"Epoch {epoch+1}/{num_epochs}: "
              f"Loss = {avg_loss:.4f}, "
              f"Sparsity = {sparsity:.2f}%, "
              f"LR = {lr:.6f}")
    
    # Final analysis
    print("\nFinal Model Analysis:")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    movement_stats = pruned_model.get_movement_stats()
    
    total_params = 0
    total_zero = 0
    
    for name, stats in movement_stats.items():
        params = pruned_model.masks[name].numel()
        zeros = (pruned_model.masks[name] == 0).sum().item()
        
        total_params += params
        total_zero += zeros
        
        print(f"\n{name}:")
        print(f"  Parameters: {params:,} ({zeros:,} pruned)")
        print(f"  Sparsity: {stats['sparsity']:.2f}%")
        print(f"  Mean movement: {stats['mean_movement']:.6f}")
        print(f"  Movement ratio (pos/neg): "
              f"{stats['positive_movement']}/{stats['negative_movement']}")
    
    print(f"\nOverall Statistics:")
    print(f"  Total parameters: {total_params:,}")
    print(f"  Pruned parameters: {total_zero:,}")
    print(f"  Overall sparsity: {100.0 * total_zero / total_params:.2f}%")
    print(f"  Model compression ratio: {total_params / (total_params - total_zero):.2f}x")
    print()

# Additional Utility Functions
# ============================================================================

class SparsityAnalyzer:
    """Utility class for analyzing sparsity patterns in models."""
    
    @staticmethod
    def count_parameters(model: nn.Module) -> dict:
        """Count total and trainable parameters."""
        total_params = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())
        trainable_params = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters() 
                              if p.requires_grad)
        return {
            'total': total_params,
            'trainable': trainable_params,
            'non_trainable': total_params - trainable_params
        }
    
    @staticmethod
    def analyze_layer_sparsity(model: nn.Module) -> dict:
        """Analyze sparsity for each layer."""
        layer_stats = {}
        
        for name, param in model.named_parameters():
            if param.requires_grad:
                total = param.numel()
                zeros = (param == 0).sum().item()
                sparsity = 100.0 * zeros / total
                
                layer_stats[name] = {
                    'shape': list(param.shape),
                    'total_params': total,
                    'zero_params': zeros,
                    'sparsity': sparsity,
                    'mean': param.data.mean().item(),
                    'std': param.data.std().item(),
                    'min': param.data.min().item(),
                    'max': param.data.max().item()
                }
        
        return layer_stats
    
    @staticmethod
    def compute_compression_ratio(model: nn.Module) -> float:
        """Compute model compression ratio."""
        total = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())
        non_zero = sum((p != 0).sum().item() for p in model.parameters())
        
        if non_zero == 0:
            return float('inf')
        return total / non_zero
    
    @staticmethod
    def estimate_memory_savings(model: nn.Module, 
                               dtype: torch.dtype = torch.float32) -> dict:
        """Estimate memory savings from sparsity."""
        bytes_per_element = torch.finfo(dtype).bits // 8
        
        total_params = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())
        non_zero_params = sum((p != 0).sum().item() for p in model.parameters())
        
        # Dense storage
        dense_memory = total_params * bytes_per_element
        
        # Sparse storage (CSR format approximation)
        # Need to store: values + column indices + row pointers
        sparse_memory = (non_zero_params * bytes_per_element +  # values
                        non_zero_params * 4 +  # column indices (int32)
                        total_params * 4 // non_zero_params if non_zero_params > 0 else 0)  # row pointers
        
        return {
            'dense_memory_mb': dense_memory / (1024 ** 2),
            'sparse_memory_mb': sparse_memory / (1024 ** 2),
            'memory_savings_mb': (dense_memory - sparse_memory) / (1024 ** 2),
            'memory_reduction_ratio': dense_memory / sparse_memory if sparse_memory > 0 else float('inf')
        }


class SparsityVisualizer:
    """Utility class for visualizing sparsity patterns."""
    
    @staticmethod
    def print_sparsity_matrix(tensor: torch.Tensor, max_size: int = 20):
        """Print a visual representation of sparsity pattern."""
        if len(tensor.shape) > 2:
            tensor = tensor.view(tensor.shape[0], -1)
        
        h, w = tensor.shape
        if h > max_size or w > max_size:
            print(f"Tensor too large ({h}x{w}), showing {max_size}x{max_size} subset")
            tensor = tensor[:max_size, :max_size]
            h, w = tensor.shape
        
        print("Sparsity Pattern (█ = non-zero, · = zero):")
        for i in range(h):
            row = ""
            for j in range(w):
                row += "█" if tensor[i, j] != 0 else "·"
            print(row)
    
    @staticmethod
    def print_sparsity_histogram(model: nn.Module, bins: int = 10):
        """Print histogram of weight magnitudes."""
        all_weights = []
        for param in model.parameters():
            if param.requires_grad:
                all_weights.append(param.data.abs().view(-1))
        
        all_weights = torch.cat(all_weights)
        non_zero_weights = all_weights[all_weights > 0]
        
        if len(non_zero_weights) == 0:
            print("All weights are zero!")
            return
        
        min_val = non_zero_weights.min().item()
        max_val = non_zero_weights.max().item()
        
        print(f"\nWeight Magnitude Histogram (non-zero weights):")
        print(f"Range: [{min_val:.6f}, {max_val:.6f}]")
        print("-" * 60)
        
        hist = torch.histc(non_zero_weights, bins=bins, min=min_val, max=max_val)
        max_count = hist.max().item()
        
        for i in range(bins):
            lower = min_val + i * (max_val - min_val) / bins
            upper = min_val + (i + 1) * (max_val - min_val) / bins
            count = hist[i].item()
            bar_length = int(40 * count / max_count) if max_count > 0 else 0
            bar = "█" * bar_length
            print(f"[{lower:.4f}, {upper:.4f}): {bar} {int(count)}")


def save_sparse_model(model: nn.Module, filepath: str, 
                      format: str = 'pytorch'):
    """
    Save model in sparse format.
    
    Args:
        model: Model to save
        filepath: Path to save file
        format: 'pytorch' or 'onnx'
    """
    if format == 'pytorch':
        # Convert dense tensors to sparse
        sparse_state_dict = {}
        for name, param in model.state_dict().items():
            if param.dtype in [torch.float32, torch.float16, torch.float64]:
                # Convert to sparse COO format
                sparse_state_dict[name] = param.to_sparse()
            else:
                sparse_state_dict[name] = param
        
        torch.save(sparse_state_dict, filepath)
        print(f"Model saved in sparse format to {filepath}")
        
    elif format == 'onnx':
        print("ONNX export would require additional setup")
        # Would need dummy input and onnx library
        pass


def load_sparse_model(model: nn.Module, filepath: str) -> nn.Module:
    """
    Load model from sparse format.
    
    Args:
        model: Model architecture
        filepath: Path to saved file
    
    Returns:
        Model with loaded weights
    """
    sparse_state_dict = torch.load(filepath)
    
    # Convert sparse tensors back to dense
    dense_state_dict = {}
    for name, param in sparse_state_dict.items():
        if param.is_sparse:
            dense_state_dict[name] = param.to_dense()
        else:
            dense_state_dict[name] = param
    
    model.load_state_dict(dense_state_dict)
    print(f"Model loaded from {filepath}")
    return model

class SparsityBenchmark:
    """Benchmark different sparsity patterns."""
    
    @staticmethod
    def benchmark_inference_speed(models: dict, input_shape: tuple, 
                                  num_iterations: int = 100):
        """Benchmark inference speed of different sparse models."""
        import time
        
        results = {}
        x = torch.randn(*input_shape)
        
        print("\nInference Speed Benchmark:")
        print("-" * 60)
        
        for name, model in models.items():
            model.eval()
            
            # Warmup
            with torch.no_grad():
                for _ in range(10):
                    _ = model(x)
            
            # Benchmark
            start_time = time.time()
            with torch.no_grad():
                for _ in range(num_iterations):
                    _ = model(x)
            end_time = time.time()
            
            avg_time = (end_time - start_time) / num_iterations * 1000  # ms
            results[name] = avg_time
            
            print(f"{name:<20}: {avg_time:.4f} ms/iteration")
        
        return results
    
    @staticmethod
    def benchmark_training_speed(models: dict, input_shape: tuple, 
                                num_classes: int = 10,
                                num_iterations: int = 50):
        """Benchmark training speed of different sparse models."""
        import time
        
        results = {}
        criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
        
        print("\nTraining Speed Benchmark:")
        print("-" * 60)
        
        for name, model in models.items():
            model.train()
            optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.001)
            
            # Warmup
            for _ in range(5):
                x = torch.randn(*input_shape)
                y = torch.randint(0, num_classes, (input_shape[0],))
                optimizer.zero_grad()
                output = model(x)
                loss = criterion(output, y)
                loss.backward()
                optimizer.step()
            
            # Benchmark
            start_time = time.time()
            for _ in range(num_iterations):
                x = torch.randn(*input_shape)
                y = torch.randint(0, num_classes, (input_shape[0],))
                optimizer.zero_grad()
                output = model(x)
                loss = criterion(output, y)
                loss.backward()
                optimizer.step()
            end_time = time.time()
            
            avg_time = (end_time - start_time) / num_iterations * 1000  # ms
            results[name] = avg_time
            
            print(f"{name:<20}: {avg_time:.4f} ms/iteration")
        
        return results

def complete_sparsity_pipeline():
    """Demonstrate a complete sparsity training pipeline."""
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("COMPLETE SPARSITY PIPELINE EXAMPLE")
    print("=" * 80 + "\n")
    
    # 1. Create model
    print("Step 1: Creating model...")
    model = create_sample_model()
    analyzer = SparsityAnalyzer()
    
    initial_stats = analyzer.count_parameters(model)
    print(f"Initial parameters: {initial_stats['total']:,}")
    
    # 2. Apply sparsity pattern
    print("\nStep 2: Applying Movement Pruning...")
    sparse_model = MovementPruningPattern(
        model,
        initial_sparsity=0.0,
        final_sparsity=0.90,
        initial_warmup=5
    )
    
    # 3. Train with sparsity
    print("\nStep 3: Training with sparsity...")
    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(sparse_model.model.parameters(), lr=0.001)
    criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
    
    total_steps = 30
    for step in range(total_steps):
        x = torch.randn(32, 784)
        y = torch.randint(0, 10, (32,))
        
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        output = sparse_model(x)
        loss = criterion(output, y)
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
        
        sparse_model.step_pruning(step, total_steps, momentum=0.9)
        
        if step % 10 == 0:
            sparsity = sparse_model.get_sparsity()
            print(f"  Step {step}: Loss = {loss.item():.4f}, Sparsity = {sparsity:.2f}%")
    
    # 4. Analyze results
    print("\nStep 4: Analyzing results...")
    final_sparsity = sparse_model.get_sparsity()
    compression_ratio = analyzer.compute_compression_ratio(sparse_model.model)
    memory_stats = analyzer.estimate_memory_savings(sparse_model.model)
    
    print(f"\nFinal Statistics:")
    print(f"  Sp
arsity: {final_sparsity:.2f}%")
    print(f"  Compression ratio: {compression_ratio:.2f}x")
    print(f"  Dense memory: {memory_stats['dense_memory_mb']:.2f} MB")
    print(f"  Sparse memory: {memory_stats['sparse_memory_mb']:.2f} MB")
    print(f"  Memory savings: {memory_stats['memory_savings_mb']:.2f} MB")
    
    # 5. Visualize sparsity
    print("\nStep 5: Visualizing sparsity pattern...")
    visualizer = SparsityVisualizer()
    
    # Get first linear layer
    first_layer = None
    for module in sparse_model.model.modules():
        if isinstance(module, nn.Linear):
            first_layer = module
            break
    
    if first_layer is not None:
        print("\nFirst layer weight sparsity pattern (20x20 subset):")
        visualizer.print_sparsity_matrix(first_layer.weight.data, max_size=20)
    
    # Print histogram
    visualizer.print_sparsity_histogram(sparse_model.model, bins=10)
    
    # 6. Layer-wise analysis
    print("\nStep 6: Layer-wise sparsity analysis...")
    layer_stats = analyzer.analyze_layer_sparsity(sparse_model.model)
    
    print("\nPer-layer statistics:")
    print("-" * 80)
    print(f"{'Layer':<30} {'Shape':<20} {'Sparsity':<15} {'Mean':<15}")
    print("-" * 80)
    for name, stats in layer_stats.items():
        shape_str = str(stats['shape'])
        print(f"{name:<30} {shape_str:<20} {stats['sparsity']:>6.2f}%{'':<8} "
              f"{stats['mean']:>8.6f}")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PIPELINE COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY")
    print("=" * 80)

        guidelines = """
        ╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
        ║                    SPARSITY INDUCTION BEST PRACTICES                       ║
        ╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
        
        1. CHOOSING A SPARSITY PATTERN:
           • L1 Sparsity: Good starting point, simple to implement
           • Group Sparsity: Use when you need structured pruning
           • Structured Sparsity: Best for deployment on standard hardware
           • Learned Sparsity: Use when you have compute budget for meta-learning
           • Magnitude Pruning: Proven baseline, works well in practice
           • Movement Pruning: State-of-the-art, best accuracy-sparsity tradeoff
        
        2. SPARSITY TARGETS:
           • Start conservative (30-50% sparsity)
           • Gradually increase to 70-90% for large models
           • Monitor accuracy degradation carefully
           • Different layers can have different sparsity levels
        
        3. TRAINING SCHEDULE:
           • Use warmup period before starting pruning (5-10% of training)
           • Gradual pruning works better than one-shot
           • Polynomial schedule often works best
           • Continue training after reaching target sparsity
        
        4. FINE-TUNING:
           • Always fine-tune after pruning
           • Use lower learning rate for fine-tuning
           • Consider learning rate rewinding techniques
           • Monitor validation metrics closely
        
        5. LAYER-WISE CONSIDERATIONS:
           • First and last layers are often more sensitive
           • Consider lower sparsity for these layers
           • Batch normalization layers usually kept dense
           • Embedding layers can often be highly sparse
        
        6. HARDWARE DEPLOYMENT:
           • Structured sparsity for CPUs/GPUs
           • Unstructured sparsity needs specialized hardware
           • Consider block sparsity (4:8, 2:4 patterns) for modern GPUs
           • Measure actual speedup, not just parameter count
        
        7. DEBUGGING TIPS:
           • Check gradient flow through sparse layers
           • Monitor sparsity distribution across layers
           • Verify masks are being applied correctly
           • Test inference speed early
        
        8. COMMON PITFALLS:
           • Pruning too aggressively too fast
           • Not fine-tuning enough after pruning
           • Ignoring batch normalization statistics
